🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #8 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 Chennai Regional Passport Office notice led to CJP’s Saurav Das being stopped at Delhi airport

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 01:17:16 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Saurav Das was served the notice at 7.30 p.m. by email on November 23, hours before his flight; the government has not issued any statement on the reasons for stopping him at the Delhi airport

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Saurav Das, co-convenor of the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), was stopped from boarding a flight to London at Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International Airport (IGI) on Monday night (November 23, 2026) after failing to respond to a show-cause notice issued by the Regional Passport Office (RPO), Chennai, over alleged discrepancies between his passport and other identity documents, a senior government official told The Hindu . His passport was issued in 2019 and the notice was served at 7.30 p.m. by email on November 23, hours before he was to board the flight at 1 a.m. on November 24. The government has issued no official statement on the reasons for stopping him at the airport. According to the notice, the RPO, Chennai, said that it has received inputs about Mr. Das’ passport application dated August 8, 2019, stating that “particulars (place of birth) furnished in it are incorrect” and his passport dated August 21, 2019 was “obtained by material suppression of facts.” “You are hereby called upon to provide a suitable clarification with respect to your place of birth along with supporting documents within seven days. Failure to produce a satisfactory response or a lack of response may result in impounding of your passport under Section 10(3)(b) of the Passports Act, 1967. You are advised not to use this passport till submission of response,” the notice seen by The Hindu said. Mr. Das said he saw the email with a show-cause notice about “discrepancies” in his passport only after he was stopped at the immigration counter at the Delhi airport. “I have no issue in providing any explanation. But I only received a show-cause notice five hours prior to my flight scheduled at 1 a.m. I did not see it before I was stopped at the airport. It says they have received an input over mismatch in my data. Can a citizen be stopped from travelling on such an input without disclosing any details of it?” He questioned why no issue was flagged in the verification process when an Indian passport was issued to him in 2019. “I have travelled abroad twice since without being stopped. The issue is being raised this time because I am associated with the CJP movement. My place of birth, my parents are being dragged into this. But we are not scared of cheap tactics.” The notice followed a September 30 order by the Madras High Court , which acted on a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) petition seeking a probe by the Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) into the nationality of Mr. Das and sought to cancel his passport and Aadhaar card if he is not found to be an Indian. The First Division Bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan also ordered notice to Mr. Das on the PIL petition filed by R. Ganesh Kumar, a businessman from Chennai. The official said that Mr. Das was asked to explain why his passport should not be impounded, as there is a mismatch in documents submitted to obtain his passport and Aadhaar. “There appears to be a mismatch regarding his date of birth, place of birth and name of father in various documents — Aadhaar, birth certificate and passport. He was asked by the RPO, Chennai to explain his stance but he did not, following which his passport was flagged and he was stopped by the immigration,” said the official.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Addressing a press conference in Delhi, Mr. Das said, “Let alone being stopped from going abroad, we have not been allowed to speak inside the country. We were stopped from going to Jantar Mantar and then Ramlila Maidan. When we took to online spaces, attempts to stop were made even there.”

articles.title: Karthigai deepam lit only at traditional spot atop Thirupparankundram hills
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Madurai Collector submitted before the Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court that the administration was taking steps to comply with the Supreme Court order

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Defying the Supreme Court’s direction to allow, as a “limited one-time arrangement”, the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at the newly identified deepathoon on Thirupparankundram hillock, the ceremonial lamp was on Tuesday lit only at the traditional spot. Earlier in the day, the Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court had recorded an undertaking by Madurai Collector Nishant Krishna that he will continue to act in strict compliance with the Supreme Court’s orders. The failure to fulfil this undertaking triggered massive protest by the leaders and cadres of the BJP and Hindu outfits at the foothills, while the ruling TVK’s allies, including the Left parties, the VCK, and the MDMK, hailed the government for sticking to tradition. “The Karthigai Mahadeepam has been lit in the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchchipillaiyar Temple located directly above the head of the presiding deity at Thirupparankundram,” Law Minister C.T.R. Nirmal Kumar said in a social media post. Shortly after the Deepam was lit, the Executive Officer of Arulmigu Subramaniya Swamy Temple, G. Selvi, and Board of Trustees Chairman V. Shanmugasundaram, in a joint press release, said the temple followed the age-old practice and agama rules in lighting the lamp. The Board of Trustees, including C. Rajapandian, K. Alagappan, K. Regina Devi, and K. Chitra, passed a resolution unanimously, resolving to follow the rituals and ensure the festival is conducted in a peaceful environment. The press release said the temple, known as the first abode of Lord Muruga (Arupadai Veedu), had been following the rituals from time immemorial. The temple, which has been conducting various festivals all through the year, adopted custom and rituals and age old continued practice as per the agama rules. In line with this, the Deepam was lit as per the old practice at the designated deepa mandapam atop the Uchipillayar temple and the light was lit at 6 p.m., the release said. The district administration, in a statement, said all arrangements were made as directed by the Supreme Court. The temple Devasthanam was requested, instructed in writing, and reminded to authorise its team and proceed. However, the Devasthanam did not authorise a team till the last moment. Instead, its Board of Trustees passed a resolution to light the lamp at the usual place, and the lamp was lit at the Deepa Mandapam, it added. Earlier, the police detained several senior leaders of the BJP, including State president Nainar Nagenthran, and Hindu outfits to prevent them from proceeding to Thirupparankundram.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Thousands of police personnel, deployed for security at the foothills, detained protesters and took them away. A section of the protesters damaged buses and other public property.

articles.newspaperPrintHtml:
🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #9 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 Karthigai deepam lit only at traditional spot atop Thirupparankundram hills

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 01:12:50 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Madurai Collector submitted before the Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court that the administration was taking steps to comply with the Supreme Court order

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Defying the Supreme Court’s direction to allow, as a “limited one-time arrangement”, the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at the newly identified deepathoon on Thirupparankundram hillock, the ceremonial lamp was on Tuesday lit only at the traditional spot. Earlier in the day, the Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court had recorded an undertaking by Madurai Collector Nishant Krishna that he will continue to act in strict compliance with the Supreme Court’s orders. The failure to fulfil this undertaking triggered massive protest by the leaders and cadres of the BJP and Hindu outfits at the foothills, while the ruling TVK’s allies, including the Left parties, the VCK, and the MDMK, hailed the government for sticking to tradition. “The Karthigai Mahadeepam has been lit in the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchchipillaiyar Temple located directly above the head of the presiding deity at Thirupparankundram,” Law Minister C.T.R. Nirmal Kumar said in a social media post. Shortly after the Deepam was lit, the Executive Officer of Arulmigu Subramaniya Swamy Temple, G. Selvi, and Board of Trustees Chairman V. Shanmugasundaram, in a joint press release, said the temple followed the age-old practice and agama rules in lighting the lamp. The Board of Trustees, including C. Rajapandian, K. Alagappan, K. Regina Devi, and K. Chitra, passed a resolution unanimously, resolving to follow the rituals and ensure the festival is conducted in a peaceful environment. The press release said the temple, known as the first abode of Lord Muruga (Arupadai Veedu), had been following the rituals from time immemorial. The temple, which has been conducting various festivals all through the year, adopted custom and rituals and age old continued practice as per the agama rules. In line with this, the Deepam was lit as per the old practice at the designated deepa mandapam atop the Uchipillayar temple and the light was lit at 6 p.m., the release said. The district administration, in a statement, said all arrangements were made as directed by the Supreme Court. The temple Devasthanam was requested, instructed in writing, and reminded to authorise its team and proceed. However, the Devasthanam did not authorise a team till the last moment. Instead, its Board of Trustees passed a resolution to light the lamp at the usual place, and the lamp was lit at the Deepa Mandapam, it added. Earlier, the police detained several senior leaders of the BJP, including State president Nainar Nagenthran, and Hindu outfits to prevent them from proceeding to Thirupparankundram.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Thousands of police personnel, deployed for security at the foothills, detained protesters and took them away. A section of the protesters damaged buses and other public property.

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: Madurai Collector submitted before the Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court that the administration was taking steps to comply with the Supreme Court order
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Defying the Supreme Court’s direction to allow, as a “limited one-time arrangement”, the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at the newly identified deepathoon on Thirupparankundram hillock, the ceremonial lamp was on Tuesday lit only at the traditional spot. Earlier in the day, the Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court had recorded an undertaking by Madurai Collector Nishant Krishna that he will continue to act in strict compliance with the Supreme Court’s orders. The failure to fulfil this undertaking triggered massive protest by the leaders and cadres of the BJP and Hindu outfits at the foothills, while the ruling TVK’s allies, including the Left parties, the VCK, and the MDMK, hailed the government for sticking to tradition. “The Karthigai Mahadeepam has been lit in the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchchipillaiyar Temple located directly above the head of the presiding deity at Thirupparankundram,” Law Minister C.T.R. Nirmal Kumar said in a social media post. Shortly after the Deepam was lit, the Executive Officer of Arulmigu Subramaniya Swamy Temple, G. Selvi, and Board of Trustees Chairman V. Shanmugasundaram, in a joint press release, said the temple followed the age-old practice and agama rules in lighting the lamp. The Board of Trustees, including C. Rajapandian, K. Alagappan, K. Regina Devi, and K. Chitra, passed a resolution unanimously, resolving to follow the rituals and ensure the festival is conducted in a peaceful environment. The press release said the temple, known as the first abode of Lord Muruga (Arupadai Veedu), had been following the rituals from time immemorial. The temple, which has been conducting various festivals all through the year, adopted custom and rituals and age old continued practice as per the agama rules. In line with this, the Deepam was lit as per the old practice at the designated deepa mandapam atop the Uchipillayar temple and the light was lit at 6 p.m., the release said. The district administration, in a statement, said all arrangements were made as directed by the Supreme Court. The temple Devasthanam was requested, instructed in writing, and reminded to authorise its team and proceed. However, the Devasthanam did not authorise a team till the last moment. Instead, its Board of Trustees passed a resolution to light the lamp at the usual place, and the lamp was lit at the Deepa Mandapam, it added. Earlier, the police detained several senior leaders of the BJP, including State president Nainar Nagenthran, and Hindu outfits to prevent them from proceeding to Thirupparankundram.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Thousands of police personnel, deployed for security at the foothills, detained protesters and took them away. A section of the protesters damaged buses and other public property.

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: We The Leaders founder K. Annamalai had criticised the TVK-led government for the delay in filling the crucial post

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Tamil Nadu government has appointed T. Tamizhselvi as vice-chairperson of the Cauvery Technical Cell-cum-Inter-State Waters Wing, Chennai. She was serving as Chief Engineer of the State Ground and Surface Water Resources Centre, Taramani. A Government Order to this effect was issued by the Water Resources Department on Tuesday. The appointment was made following orders approving the revival of the post and filling the vacant permanent position of vice-chairperson in the Cauvery Technical Cell-cum-Inter-State Waters Wing at the level of Chief Engineer. The post had been vacant since January 28 this year, following the resignation of M. Selvaraj.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Recently, We The Leaders founder K. Annamalai had criticised the TVK-led government for the delay in filling the crucial post.

📰 Tamizhselvi named vice-chairperson of Cauvery Technical Cell-cum-Inter-State Waters Wing

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 01:10:04 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: We The Leaders founder K. Annamalai had criticised the TVK-led government for the delay in filling the crucial post

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Tamil Nadu government has appointed T. Tamizhselvi as vice-chairperson of the Cauvery Technical Cell-cum-Inter-State Waters Wing, Chennai. She was serving as Chief Engineer of the State Ground and Surface Water Resources Centre, Taramani. A Government Order to this effect was issued by the Water Resources Department on Tuesday. The appointment was made following orders approving the revival of the post and filling the vacant permanent position of vice-chairperson in the Cauvery Technical Cell-cum-Inter-State Waters Wing at the level of Chief Engineer. The post had been vacant since January 28 this year, following the resignation of M. Selvaraj.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Recently, We The Leaders founder K. Annamalai had criticised the TVK-led government for the delay in filling the crucial post.

articles.title: Plans afoot to onboard all tourism products on NDTS
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: To help tourists enjoy a hassle-free stay and travel in the State, plans are afoot to onboard all tourism products and experiences on the National Digital Tourism Stack (NDTS).

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: “The idea is to onboard all tourism products and experiences in the National tourism stack. Tourists can book rooms, tickets to sites, tours, train and bus tickets, learn about facilities at sites, get details of timings and dos and don’ts etc., via this stack. Places that don’t have online ticketing will also be included so that anyone from anywhere can book in advance and enjoy that experience as well,” a source in the Tourism Department said

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: A meeting of officials of departments including Tourism, Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments, and Municipal Administration was convened jointly by Tamil Nadu Tourism Development Corporation and the Open Network for Digital Commerce, said a press release here.

articles.title: Wall Street roars back as Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Nvidia shares surged 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after an extraordinary reversal, which followed President Donald Trump’s call for Jensen Huang’s return

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Wall Street’s main indexes rallied sharply on Monday (November 23, 2026), led by a ​nearly 7% jump in the tech-heavy Nasdaq, as investors rushed back into AI-linked stocks ⁠after Nvidia said it had reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive. Nvidia shares surged 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after an extraordinary reversal, which followed President Donald Trump’s call for Mr. Huang’s return. Mr. Huang resigned ‌as chief executive earlier this month over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. The chipmaker is widely regarded as a cornerstone of the AI trade, and ‌its sharp rebound helped lift sentiment across the sector after weeks of heavy selling. “Huang’s return ‌marks ⁠one of the biggest reversals in the history of the stock market. Never has so ⁠much value rested on the shoulders of a single executive,” said David Russell, global head of market strategy at TradeStation. “Wall Street envisioned a stock market without his leadership and didn’t like what it saw.” The Nasdaq-100 was on track to add more than $2 trillion ​in market value on Monday (November 23). The Nasdaq ‌Composite and the S&P 500 were on track for their biggest one-day gains since markets surged after Mr. Trump paused his “Liberation Day” tariff package in April 2025. Chip stocks gained, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index up 13.4% and also on track for its best session since April 2025.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The rally was broad-based in ‌the tech sphere, with the so-called Magnificent Seven stocks Tesla, Amazon , Microsoft, Meta and Alphabet climbing ​between 5.8% and 12.4%.

📰 Wall Street roars back as Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO

📌 Published: 24 Nov 2026, 12:26:40 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Nvidia shares surged 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after an extraordinary reversal, which followed President Donald Trump’s call for Jensen Huang’s return

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Wall Street’s main indexes rallied sharply on Monday (November 23, 2026), led by a ​nearly 7% jump in the tech-heavy Nasdaq, as investors rushed back into AI-linked stocks ⁠after Nvidia said it had reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive. Nvidia shares surged 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after an extraordinary reversal, which followed President Donald Trump’s call for Mr. Huang’s return. Mr. Huang resigned ‌as chief executive earlier this month over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. The chipmaker is widely regarded as a cornerstone of the AI trade, and ‌its sharp rebound helped lift sentiment across the sector after weeks of heavy selling. “Huang’s return ‌marks ⁠one of the biggest reversals in the history of the stock market. Never has so ⁠much value rested on the shoulders of a single executive,” said David Russell, global head of market strategy at TradeStation. “Wall Street envisioned a stock market without his leadership and didn’t like what it saw.” The Nasdaq-100 was on track to add more than $2 trillion ​in market value on Monday (November 23). The Nasdaq ‌Composite and the S&P 500 were on track for their biggest one-day gains since markets surged after Mr. Trump paused his “Liberation Day” tariff package in April 2025. Chip stocks gained, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index up 13.4% and also on track for its best session since April 2025.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The rally was broad-based in ‌the tech sphere, with the so-called Magnificent Seven stocks Tesla, Amazon , Microsoft, Meta and Alphabet climbing ​between 5.8% and 12.4%.

articles.title: Oil and gas production to pick up in 4-5 years as recent measures take effect, Petroleum Ministry says
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: In a note accessed by The Hindu, the Ministry has said that the oil and gas industry has a long gestation period and so exploration and finance decisions taken more than a decade ago are affecting the industry now

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The government expects domestic oil and gas production to pick up in the next 4-5 years as several steps taken in the recent past begin to bear fruit in an industry typically characterised by long gestation periods, The Hindu has learnt. According to an analysis by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, the current contraction in domestic oil and gas production is due to factors that took place more than a decade ago. However, since then, the government has taken steps such as increasing drilling and exploration to record levels, changing laws and rules to provide stable terms to explorers, and opening new avenues for exploration. “The steps taken in the last few years — new acreage, record drilling, deepwater wells and the revival of Mumbai High — will start showing up in production over the next three to four years,” the note asserted. “That is the nature of this sector: the decisions of one decade decide the output of the next.” The note also argues that now, unlike earlier, the profits of oil and gas companies upstream companies like ONGC and Oil India are being used to fund exploration rather than subsidies. “Until 2015, ONGC and Oil India were made to fund a large share of the subsidy on diesel, LPG and kerosene, through discounts on the crude they sold to oil marketing companies,” the note said. According to data with the Ministry, ONGC paid ₹49,421 crore towards this subsidy in 2012-13 against a profit of ₹20,926 crore, and in 2013-14 paid ₹56,384 crore towards this subsidy against a net profit of ₹22,095 crore. “In both years ONGC gave away more than twice what it earned,” the note said. “Money that should have gone into finding new oil and gas went into keeping retail prices down. This burden was ended from 2015-16. ONGC now keeps its earnings and has sharply raised its spending on exploration.” According to the latest data on the Index of Core Industries, the oil and gas sectors have contracted continuously for 22 and 28 months, respectively.

📈 Economic, Banking & Finance Paragraph #14 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Oil and gas production to pick up in 4-5 years as recent measures take effect, Petroleum Ministry says

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 08:32:08 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: In a note accessed by The Hindu, the Ministry has said that the oil and gas industry has a long gestation period and so exploration and finance decisions taken more than a decade ago are affecting the industry now

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The government expects domestic oil and gas production to pick up in the next 4-5 years as several steps taken in the recent past begin to bear fruit in an industry typically characterised by long gestation periods, The Hindu has learnt. According to an analysis by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, the current contraction in domestic oil and gas production is due to factors that took place more than a decade ago. However, since then, the government has taken steps such as increasing drilling and exploration to record levels, changing laws and rules to provide stable terms to explorers, and opening new avenues for exploration. “The steps taken in the last few years — new acreage, record drilling, deepwater wells and the revival of Mumbai High — will start showing up in production over the next three to four years,” the note asserted. “That is the nature of this sector: the decisions of one decade decide the output of the next.” The note also argues that now, unlike earlier, the profits of oil and gas companies upstream companies like ONGC and Oil India are being used to fund exploration rather than subsidies. “Until 2015, ONGC and Oil India were made to fund a large share of the subsidy on diesel, LPG and kerosene, through discounts on the crude they sold to oil marketing companies,” the note said. According to data with the Ministry, ONGC paid ₹49,421 crore towards this subsidy in 2012-13 against a profit of ₹20,926 crore, and in 2013-14 paid ₹56,384 crore towards this subsidy against a net profit of ₹22,095 crore. “In both years ONGC gave away more than twice what it earned,” the note said. “Money that should have gone into finding new oil and gas went into keeping retail prices down. This burden was ended from 2015-16. ONGC now keeps its earnings and has sharply raised its spending on exploration.” According to the latest data on the Index of Core Industries, the oil and gas sectors have contracted continuously for 22 and 28 months, respectively.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “In this sector it takes five to ten years to go from awarding a block to first production,” a note prepared by the Ministry and accessed by The Hindu said. “Output in 2026 is the result of what was, and was not, done a decade ago.

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 📈 Economic, Banking & Finance passage on "Oil and gas production to pick up in 4-5 years as recent measures take effect, Petroleum Ministry says", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. In a note accessed by The Hindu, the Ministry has said that the oil and gas industry has a long gestation period and so exploration and finance...

C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Oil and gas production to pick up in 4-5 year' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Oil and gas production to pick up in 4-5 year' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Oil and gas production to pick up in 4-5 years as recent measures take effect, Petroleum Ministry says"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. “Output in 2026 is the result of what was, and was not, done a decade ago.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "“Output in 2026 is the result of what was, and was not, done a decade ago." (Hinglish Arth: “2026 में आउटपुट एक दशक पहले जो किया गया था और जो नहीं किया गया था उसका परिणाम है।)

articles.title: SBI, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank retain D-SIB status; RBI maintains capital requirements
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The additional capital requirements are intended to enhance the resilience of these institutions.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has retained State Bank of India (SBI), HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank in its 2026 list of Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs), maintaining their respective positions under the same bucketing structure as in 2025. Under the RBI’s framework, SBI, placed in Bucket 4, will have to maintain an additional Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital requirement of 0.80% of its Risk Weighted Assets (RWAs). HDFC Bank, classified under Bucket 2, will have an additional CET1 requirement of 0.40%, while ICICI Bank, placed in Bucket 1, will have to maintain 0.20%. These additional capital requirements are over and above the Capital Conservation Buffer, strengthening the banks’ ability to absorb financial shocks and contain systemic risks. The latest classification is based on data collected from banks as of March 31, 2026. Under the D-SIB framework, banks are categorised into different buckets according to their Systemic Importance Scores (SISs), with higher scores attracting higher additional capital requirements. The RBI introduced the Framework for Dealing with D-SIBs on July 22, 2014, subsequently updating it on December 28, 2023. The framework requires the central bank to publicly disclose the names of designated D-SIBs annually, beginning in 2015, and assign them to appropriate buckets based on their systemic importance. SBI and ICICI Bank were initially designated as D-SIBs in 2015 and 2016, respectively. HDFC Bank joined the list in 2017, when all three banks were identified as systemically important financial institutions.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: economy (general) / business (general) / banking / Reserve Bank of India / financial and business service

📈 Economic, Banking & Finance Paragraph #15 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 SBI, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank retain D-SIB status; RBI maintains capital requirements

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 07:16:07 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The additional capital requirements are intended to enhance the resilience of these institutions.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has retained State Bank of India (SBI), HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank in its 2026 list of Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs), maintaining their respective positions under the same bucketing structure as in 2025. Under the RBI’s framework, SBI, placed in Bucket 4, will have to maintain an additional Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital requirement of 0.80% of its Risk Weighted Assets (RWAs). HDFC Bank, classified under Bucket 2, will have an additional CET1 requirement of 0.40%, while ICICI Bank, placed in Bucket 1, will have to maintain 0.20%. These additional capital requirements are over and above the Capital Conservation Buffer, strengthening the banks’ ability to absorb financial shocks and contain systemic risks. The latest classification is based on data collected from banks as of March 31, 2026. Under the D-SIB framework, banks are categorised into different buckets according to their Systemic Importance Scores (SISs), with higher scores attracting higher additional capital requirements. The RBI introduced the Framework for Dealing with D-SIBs on July 22, 2014, subsequently updating it on December 28, 2023. The framework requires the central bank to publicly disclose the names of designated D-SIBs annually, beginning in 2015, and assign them to appropriate buckets based on their systemic importance. SBI and ICICI Bank were initially designated as D-SIBs in 2015 and 2016, respectively. HDFC Bank joined the list in 2017, when all three banks were identified as systemically important financial institutions.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: economy (general) / business (general) / banking / Reserve Bank of India / financial and business service

संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ।
✓ Syn: Systemic, Organizational, Constitutional  |  ✖ Ant: Individual, Informal, Unorganized
Resilience (Noun)
लचीलापन और मज़बूती — किसी बड़े संकट या मंदी के बाद तेज़ी से वापस उभरने की क्षमता।
✓ Syn: Robustness, Endurance, Adaptability  |  ✖ Ant: Fragility, Vulnerability, Weakness
Classification (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Classification' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Conservation (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Conservation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 📈 Economic, Banking & Finance passage on "SBI, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank retain D-SIB status; RBI maintains capital requirements", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The additional capital requirements are intended to enhance the resilience of these institutions.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'SBI, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank retain D-SIB status; ' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'SBI, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank retain D-SIB statu' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'SBI, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank retain D-SIB statu' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The additional capital requirements are intended to enhance the resilience of these institutions." (Hinglish Arth: अतिरिक्त पूंजी आवश्यकताओं का उद्देश्य इन संस्थानों की लचीलापन बढ़ाना है।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "SBI, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank retain D-SIB status; RBI maintains capital requirements"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. economy (general) / business (general) / banking / Reserve Bank of India / financial and business service.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "economy (general) / business (general) / banking / Reserve Bank of India / financial and business service." fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Rampur Bushahr’s Lavi Fair in Himachal Pradesh traces a Himalayan journey from wool and barter to women entrepreneurs and digital payments

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: What Disneyland is to children today, Lavi Fair in Rampur Bushahr, in Himachal Pradesh’s Shimla district, was to my family in the 1980s. I recall wandering through the fair as an eight-year-old, watching an old man smoking a chillum beside heaps of black sheep fleece and stacks of white woollen pattus (traditional garments of Kinnaur and Kullu women). Mother and her friends carefully chose shawls for their daughters’ and future daughters-in-law’s trousseaux. Years later, I received a beautiful black sheep wool and pashmina shawl for my wedding. Wool finds pride of place at the fair. The name Lavi is linked to “Loe”, a sheet of woollen cloth and the practice of shearing sheep.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Hindu Sunday Magazine / trade policy / trade dispute / trade agreements / international (foreign) trade / Himachal Pradesh / economy / business (general) / taxes and duties / travelogues / travel and commuting

articles.title: Must balance ‘economic patriotism’ with cultural heritage: GJC on PM Modi’s call to stop gold purchases
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) argued that the gold jewellery sector contributes nearly 7-8% to the economy and supports millions of livelihoods

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: While welcoming Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for prioritising locally-made products and reducing gold imports, the All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) has said that India must balance “economic patriotism” and its cultural traditions when it comes to gold jewellery. It argued that the sector contributes “nearly 7-8%” to the economy and supports “millions of livelihoods”. The GJC was reacting to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s recent and repeated appeal to all Indians to stop foreign trips and weddings, to buy local, and to only buy gold if necessary. “The Prime Minister’s appeal for economic patriotism and greater preference for Swadeshi products is timely and welcome,” Rajesh Rokde, Chairman of the All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) said. “While we fully support the Prime Minister’s call for restraint when gold is viewed purely as bullion or an investment instrument, jewellery consumption remains closely linked to culture, craftsmanship, and livelihoods,” Mr. Rokde added. He said that gold and jewellery hold a unique place in India’s cultural heritage, particularly during festive and wedding seasons, such as the period that India will soon enter in October-December. “The jewellery industry, contributing nearly 7-8% to the economy and supporting millions of livelihoods, is an integral part of India’s growth story,” Mr. Rokde asserted. ‘People bought less gold, prices fell’: Modi recalls year-old appeal

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “As a ₹10 lakh crore industry, the Indian jewellery sector must continue to grow responsibly, with greater transparency, value creation, and alignment with national priorities — balancing economic patriotism with India’s enduring cultural traditions,” he added.

📈 Economic, Banking & Finance Paragraph #17 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 Must balance ‘economic patriotism’ with cultural heritage: GJC on PM Modi’s call to stop gold purchases

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 01:31:24 AM IST
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) argued that the gold jewellery sector contributes nearly 7-8% to the economy and supports millions of livelihoods

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: While welcoming Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for prioritising locally-made products and reducing gold imports, the All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) has said that India must balance “economic patriotism” and its cultural traditions when it comes to gold jewellery. It argued that the sector contributes “nearly 7-8%” to the economy and supports “millions of livelihoods”. The GJC was reacting to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s recent and repeated appeal to all Indians to stop foreign trips and weddings, to buy local, and to only buy gold if necessary. “The Prime Minister’s appeal for economic patriotism and greater preference for Swadeshi products is timely and welcome,” Rajesh Rokde, Chairman of the All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) said. “While we fully support the Prime Minister’s call for restraint when gold is viewed purely as bullion or an investment instrument, jewellery consumption remains closely linked to culture, craftsmanship, and livelihoods,” Mr. Rokde added. He said that gold and jewellery hold a unique place in India’s cultural heritage, particularly during festive and wedding seasons, such as the period that India will soon enter in October-December. “The jewellery industry, contributing nearly 7-8% to the economy and supporting millions of livelihoods, is an integral part of India’s growth story,” Mr. Rokde asserted. ‘People bought less gold, prices fell’: Modi recalls year-old appeal

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “As a ₹10 lakh crore industry, the Indian jewellery sector must continue to grow responsibly, with greater transparency, value creation, and alignment with national priorities — balancing economic patriotism with India’s enduring cultural traditions,” he added.

निवेश — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Investment' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

D. The author contends that 'Must balance ‘economic patriotism’ with cultu' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.

Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Must balance ‘economic patriotism’ with cultural heritage: GJC on PM Modi’s call to stop gold purchases"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. “As a ₹10 lakh crore industry, the Indian jewellery sector must continue to grow responsibly, with greater transparency, value creation, and...
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "“As a ₹10 lakh crore industry, the Indian jewellery sector must continue to grow responsibly, with greater transparency, value creation, and..." (Hinglish Arth: “₹10 लाख करोड़ के उद्योग के रूप में, भारतीय आभूषण क्षेत्र को अधिक पारदर्शिता, मूल्य सृजन और राष्ट्रीय प्राथमिकताओं के साथ संरेखण के साथ जिम्मेदारी से बढ़ना जारी रखना चाहिए – भारत की आर्थिक देशभक्ति के साथ संतुलन बनाना चाहिए।”)

articles.title: India, Finland seek to deepen economic ties through startup cooperation: Envoy Mikko Kivikoski
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: "We want to engage more with the Indian startup actors. And here we see the startup sector, startup ecosystems, as an important part of that cooperation," Mikki Kivikoski said

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: “India and Finland are looking to deepen economic cooperation by strengthening ties between their startup ecosystems and promoting greater two-way investment,” Finnish Ambassador to India Mikko Kivikoski has said. "We want to engage more with the Indian startup actors. And of course, at the end of the day, this is all about advancing the economic cooperation between our countries. And here we see the startup sector, startup ecosystems, as an important part of that cooperation," Mr. Kivikoski told PTI . The Ambassador was speaking at an unconventional startup event held at the Embassy of Finland in New Delhi on Friday (November 20, 2026), where entrepreneurs stepped into an ice-cold pool to pitch their ideas, drawing on Finland's winter-swimming tradition. "We have quite a long tradition in Finland for these kinds of events," Mr. Kivikoski said. "This year has been record-high when it comes to interaction and engagement between Finland and India," he said, referring to visits by the Finnish Prime Minister and President, as well as meetings between the leaders of the two countries. The Ambassador said the two sides agreed to elevate their bilateral relationship to a Strategic Partnership in Digitalisation and Sustainability during Finnish President Alexander Stubb's state visit to India in March. Prime Minister Narendra Modi met his Finnish counterpart, Petteri Orpo, in New Delhi on the sidelines of the AI Impact Summit in February and in Oslo on the margins of the 3rd India-Nordic Summit in May. Mr. Kivikoski also referred to the visits to Finland by India's External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal during the summer. "We see India as a trusted partner when it comes to the Indo-Pacific area," he said. The Ambassador said the India-Finland relationship was increasingly moving beyond conventional trade towards a partnership involving investments and people-to-people exchanges. "What we are seeing already, and what is happening between the European Union and India and between India and Finland, is that we are now talking about partnership. It's not anymore about me selling something to you and you selling something to me," he said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: "There are more and more Finnish companies coming to the Indian market and more and more Indian companies going to the Finnish market. And of course we hope, and we are confident, that this dynamism will continue in the future," he said.

📈 Economic, Banking & Finance Paragraph #18 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 India, Finland seek to deepen economic ties through startup cooperation: Envoy Mikko Kivikoski

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 01:31:24 AM IST
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: "We want to engage more with the Indian startup actors. And here we see the startup sector, startup ecosystems, as an important part of that cooperation," Mikki Kivikoski said

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: “India and Finland are looking to deepen economic cooperation by strengthening ties between their startup ecosystems and promoting greater two-way investment,” Finnish Ambassador to India Mikko Kivikoski has said. "We want to engage more with the Indian startup actors. And of course, at the end of the day, this is all about advancing the economic cooperation between our countries. And here we see the startup sector, startup ecosystems, as an important part of that cooperation," Mr. Kivikoski told PTI . The Ambassador was speaking at an unconventional startup event held at the Embassy of Finland in New Delhi on Friday (November 20, 2026), where entrepreneurs stepped into an ice-cold pool to pitch their ideas, drawing on Finland's winter-swimming tradition. "We have quite a long tradition in Finland for these kinds of events," Mr. Kivikoski said. "This year has been record-high when it comes to interaction and engagement between Finland and India," he said, referring to visits by the Finnish Prime Minister and President, as well as meetings between the leaders of the two countries. The Ambassador said the two sides agreed to elevate their bilateral relationship to a Strategic Partnership in Digitalisation and Sustainability during Finnish President Alexander Stubb's state visit to India in March. Prime Minister Narendra Modi met his Finnish counterpart, Petteri Orpo, in New Delhi on the sidelines of the AI Impact Summit in February and in Oslo on the margins of the 3rd India-Nordic Summit in May. Mr. Kivikoski also referred to the visits to Finland by India's External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal during the summer. "We see India as a trusted partner when it comes to the Indo-Pacific area," he said. The Ambassador said the India-Finland relationship was increasingly moving beyond conventional trade towards a partnership involving investments and people-to-people exchanges. "What we are seeing already, and what is happening between the European Union and India and between India and Finland, is that we are now talking about partnership. It's not anymore about me selling something to you and you selling something to me," he said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: "There are more and more Finnish companies coming to the Indian market and more and more Indian companies going to the Finnish market. And of course we hope, and we are confident, that this dynamism will continue in the future," he said.

Sustainability (Noun)
सतत विकास — पर्यावरण और भविष्य की पीढ़ियों को नुकसान पहुँचाए बिना लंबे समय तक चलने वाला विकास।
✓ Syn: Viability, Eco-balance, Durability  |  ✖ Ant: Depletion, Unsustainability, Destruction
Unconventional (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Unconventional' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Digitalisation (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Digitalisation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।

And here we see the startup sector, startup ecosystems, as an important part of that cooperation," Mr. Kivikoski told PTI . The Ambassador was speaking at an unconventional startup event held at the Embassy of Finland in New Delhi on Friday (November 20, 2026), where entrepreneurs stepped into an ice-cold pool to pitch their ideas, drawing on Finland's winter-swimming tradition. Prime Minister Narendra Modi met his Finnish counterpart, Petteri Orpo, in New Delhi on the sidelines of the AI Impact Summit in February and in Oslo on the margins of the 3rd India-Nordic Summit in May. "We see India as a trusted partner when it comes to the Indo-Pacific area," he said. The Ambassador said the India-Finland relationship was increasingly moving beyond conventional trade towards a partnership involving investments and people-to-people exchanges. articles.title: Iran rules out talks with U.S. until its seven conditions are met
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Iran also said three oil tankers had struck naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz and caught fire despite U.S. aerial protection

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Iran reiterated Tuesday (November 24, 2026) that it would not hold talks with the United States to end the conflict, saying that seven conditions must be met first, though it didn't specify the conditions. Iran also said three oil tankers had struck naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz and caught fire despite U.S. aerial protection. Meanwhile, at least nine Palestinians were killed in several Israeli strikes in Gaza, local officials said. Iran's chief negotiator and Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said Tuesday (November 24, 2026) that Tehran wouldn't negotiate with the U.S. "until Iran's seven conditions are met,” according to Iranian state television. Iranian authorities haven't publicly stated what those conditions are. But Iranian state media have said they include the lifting of sanctions, the ending of the U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports and the release of seized Iranian assets. He also warned that Iran would “shift the geographical scope of the conflict should the enemy make a mistake.” The naval arm of Iran's Revolutionary Guard said the three oil tankers struck the naval mines because they were “in violation of regulations” regarding passage through the Strait of Hormuz. The Guard's navy said in a post on Telegram Monday (November 23, 2026) that the strait “is not a place to test unauthorised routes or to disregard maritime warnings.” It said the tankers were “engulfed in flames” after hitting the mines despite being under U.S. aerial escort.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: At least nine people were killed in four Israeli strikes Monday night (November 23, 2026) and Tuesday morning (November 24, 2026), officials in Gaza said. Among those killed was a senior security official in the Hamas-run government's Interior Ministry.

📰 Iran rules out talks with U.S. until its seven conditions are met

📌 Published: 24 Nov 2026, 11:06:11 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Iran also said three oil tankers had struck naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz and caught fire despite U.S. aerial protection

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Iran reiterated Tuesday (November 24, 2026) that it would not hold talks with the United States to end the conflict, saying that seven conditions must be met first, though it didn't specify the conditions. Iran also said three oil tankers had struck naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz and caught fire despite U.S. aerial protection. Meanwhile, at least nine Palestinians were killed in several Israeli strikes in Gaza, local officials said. Iran's chief negotiator and Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said Tuesday (November 24, 2026) that Tehran wouldn't negotiate with the U.S. "until Iran's seven conditions are met,” according to Iranian state television. articles.title: Former members say EPG report was ‘highly positive’ for India-Nepal ties
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Their reaction comes a day after Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri termed the report of India-Nepal Eminent Persons Group “not relevant”

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A day after Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri termed the report of the India-Nepal Eminent Persons Group (EPG) “not relevant”, arguing that India will take a “forward looking” approach regarding boundary issues with Nepal, a former member of the EPG has said the report was “highly positive” for both India and Nepal and that it was “odd” that the group did not get a chance to present the report to the Government of India. “The EPG report was produced after extensive research and field visits. We visited Visakhapatnam and other ports that are of interest to Nepal and spoke with many stakeholders before compiling the report and there are interesting recommendations in the report that could be of great use for India and Nepal and it was highly positive for Delhi-Kathmandu relations,” said Mahendra P. Lama, former professor of Jawaharlal Nehru University, who served as a member of the EPG. ALSO WATCH India-Nepal ties: What does Modi-Balen partnership promise? | Above the Fold | Nov 23, 2026 The EPG returned to the spotlight on Monday (November 23, 2026) when Mr. Misri announced in a press conference held after the visit of Nepali Prime Minister Balendra Shah that New Delhi would adopt a “forward-looking” approach to the border issues. “The leaders have given a direction as part of the overall very forward-looking discussions that have been held today for the foreign secretaries to take the task forward. We will do so in a forward-looking manner, taking inspiration from the vision document and from the directions and indeed the spirit in which the discussions were held. I would say that EPG is in the past. We are not looking backward,” said Mr. Misri in response to a question. He described the EPG report as “not relevant”. Former Nepali ambassador and coordinator of the EPG on the Nepali side, Bhek Bahadur Thapa, described the EPG report as a step forward for the bilateral consultation process. “It was not a unilateral document, it was a document created through bilateral consultation among experts appointed by New Delhi and Kathmandu,” said Mr. Thapa, who has also served as Foreign Minister of Nepal during 2004-05. The EPG report dealing with a broad spectrum of India-Nepal relations, including the Kalapani dispute and the 1950 India-Nepal Friendship Treaty was completed in 2018 but it remained under sealed covers. “It is odd that the report could not be launched here in Delhi. The Nepali side said the EPG report should be unveiled first by the Indian Prime Minister and on the same day we were supposed to return to Kathmandu for the report’s unveiling by the Nepali Prime Minister, “ said Prof. Lama, informing that they made a mistake as Kathmandu could have also unveiled the report first. “Our recommendations now can be accessed by other stakeholders in Kathmandu and I don’t think that is a positive thing,” said Mr. Lama. The EPG was institutionalised according to an understanding that was reached during the delegation-level talks between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and former Nepali Prime Minister K.P. Sharma Oli in February 2016. The visit of Mr. Oli took place against the backdrop of months-long blockade on Nepal-India border that Kathmandu said was imposed by India but India blamed the Madhesi agitators of Nepal for imposing the blockade that hindered flow of essential items such as cooking gas into Nepal. During the time of its existence, a part of the Institute of Defence Studies and Analyses (IDSA) in Delhi served as the secretariat for the EPG. The then Director General of the IDSA Jayant Prasad was also part of the EPG.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Incidentally, officials who are currently playing key roles in India-Nepal relations were also involved in the EPG process. Former members recounted that the newly appointed Indian ambassador to Nepal Sudhakar Dalela was the Joint Secretary (North) in the Ministry of External Affairs and was part of the EPG process during 2016-18. That apart, the new Nepali ambassador to India Nischal Nath Pandey also was part of the EPG process in Kathmandu.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #20 of 30 (24 NOV)

📰 Former members say EPG report was ‘highly positive’ for India-Nepal ties

📌 Published: 24 Nov 2026, 11:01:38 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Their reaction comes a day after Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri termed the report of India-Nepal Eminent Persons Group “not relevant”

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A day after Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri termed the report of the India-Nepal Eminent Persons Group (EPG) “not relevant”, arguing that India will take a “forward looking” approach regarding boundary issues with Nepal, a former member of the EPG has said the report was “highly positive” for both India and Nepal and that it was “odd” that the group did not get a chance to present the report to the Government of India. “The EPG report was produced after extensive research and field visits. We visited Visakhapatnam and other ports that are of interest to Nepal and spoke with many stakeholders before compiling the report and there are interesting recommendations in the report that could be of great use for India and Nepal and it was highly positive for Delhi-Kathmandu relations,” said Mahendra P. Lama, former professor of Jawaharlal Nehru University, who served as a member of the EPG. ALSO WATCH India-Nepal ties: What does Modi-Balen partnership promise? | Above the Fold | Nov 23, 2026 The EPG returned to the spotlight on Monday (November 23, 2026) when Mr. Misri announced in a press conference held after the visit of Nepali Prime Minister Balendra Shah that New Delhi would adopt a “forward-looking” approach to the border issues. “The leaders have given a direction as part of the overall very forward-looking discussions that have been held today for the foreign secretaries to take the task forward. We will do so in a forward-looking manner, taking inspiration from the vision document and from the directions and indeed the spirit in which the discussions were held. I would say that EPG is in the past. We are not looking backward,” said Mr. Misri in response to a question. He described the EPG report as “not relevant”. Former Nepali ambassador and coordinator of the EPG on the Nepali side, Bhek Bahadur Thapa, described the EPG report as a step forward for the bilateral consultation process. “It was not a unilateral document, it was a document created through bilateral consultation among experts appointed by New Delhi and Kathmandu,” said Mr. Thapa, who has also served as Foreign Minister of Nepal during 2004-05. The EPG report dealing with a broad spectrum of India-Nepal relations, including the Kalapani dispute and the 1950 India-Nepal Friendship Treaty was completed in 2018 but it remained under sealed covers. “It is odd that the report could not be launched here in Delhi. The Nepali side said the EPG report should be unveiled first by the Indian Prime Minister and on the same day we were supposed to return to Kathmandu for the report’s unveiling by the Nepali Prime Minister, “ said Prof. Lama, informing that they made a mistake as Kathmandu could have also unveiled the report first. “Our recommendations now can be accessed by other stakeholders in Kathmandu and I don’t think that is a positive thing,” said Mr. Lama. The EPG was institutionalised according to an understanding that was reached during the delegation-level talks between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and former Nepali Prime Minister K.P. Sharma Oli in February 2016. The visit of Mr. Oli took place against the backdrop of months-long blockade on Nepal-India border that Kathmandu said was imposed by India but India blamed the Madhesi agitators of Nepal for imposing the blockade that hindered flow of essential items such as cooking gas into Nepal. During the time of its existence, a part of the Institute of Defence Studies and Analyses (IDSA) in Delhi served as the secretariat for the EPG. The then Director General of the IDSA Jayant Prasad was also part of the EPG.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Incidentally, officials who are currently playing key roles in India-Nepal relations were also involved in the EPG process. Former members recounted that the newly appointed Indian ambassador to Nepal Sudhakar Dalela was the Joint Secretary (North) in the Ministry of External Affairs and was part of the EPG process during 2016-18. That apart, the new Nepali ambassador to India Nischal Nath Pandey also was part of the EPG process in Kathmandu.

articles.summary: 1. Core Context & Background: Their reaction comes a day after Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri termed the report of India-Nepal Eminent Persons Group “not relevant”
articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: Their reaction comes a day after Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri termed the report of India-Nepal Eminent Persons Group “not relevant”
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A day after Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri termed the report of the India-Nepal Eminent Persons Group (EPG) “not relevant”, arguing that India will take a “forward looking” approach regarding boundary issues with Nepal, a former member of the EPG has said the report was “highly positive” for both India and Nepal and that it was “odd” that the group did not get a chance to present the report to the Government of India. “The EPG report was produced after extensive research and field visits. We visited Visakhapatnam and other ports that are of interest to Nepal and spoke with many stakeholders before compiling the report and there are interesting recommendations in the report that could be of great use for India and Nepal and it was highly positive for Delhi-Kathmandu relations,” said Mahendra P. Lama, former professor of Jawaharlal Nehru University, who served as a member of the EPG. ALSO WATCH India-Nepal ties: What does Modi-Balen partnership promise? | Above the Fold | Nov 23, 2026 The EPG returned to the spotlight on Monday (November 23, 2026) when Mr. Misri announced in a press conference held after the visit of Nepali Prime Minister Balendra Shah that New Delhi would adopt a “forward-looking” approach to the border issues. “The leaders have given a direction as part of the overall very forward-looking discussions that have been held today for the foreign secretaries to take the task forward. We will do so in a forward-looking manner, taking inspiration from the vision document and from the directions and indeed the spirit in which the discussions were held. I would say that EPG is in the past. We are not looking backward,” said Mr. Misri in response to a question. He described the EPG report as “not relevant”. Former Nepali ambassador and coordinator of the EPG on the Nepali side, Bhek Bahadur Thapa, described the EPG report as a step forward for the bilateral consultation process. “It was not a unilateral document, it was a document created through bilateral consultation among experts appointed by New Delhi and Kathmandu,” said Mr. Thapa, who has also served as Foreign Minister of Nepal during 2004-05. The EPG report dealing with a broad spectrum of India-Nepal relations, including the Kalapani dispute and the 1950 India-Nepal Friendship Treaty was completed in 2018 but it remained under sealed covers. “It is odd that the report could not be launched here in Delhi. The Nepali side said the EPG report should be unveiled first by the Indian Prime Minister and on the same day we were supposed to return to Kathmandu for the report’s unveiling by the Nepali Prime Minister, “ said Prof. Lama, informing that they made a mistake as Kathmandu could have also unveiled the report first. “Our recommendations now can be accessed by other stakeholders in Kathmandu and I don’t think that is a positive thing,” said Mr. Lama. The EPG was institutionalised according to an understanding that was reached during the delegation-level talks between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and former Nepali Prime Minister K.P. Sharma Oli in February 2016. The visit of Mr. Oli took place against the backdrop of months-long blockade on Nepal-India border that Kathmandu said was imposed by India but India blamed the Madhesi agitators of Nepal for imposing the blockade that hindered flow of essential items such as cooking gas into Nepal. During the time of its existence, a part of the Institute of Defence Studies and Analyses (IDSA) in Delhi served as the secretariat for the EPG. The then Director General of the IDSA Jayant Prasad was also part of the EPG.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Incidentally, officials who are currently playing key roles in India-Nepal relations were also involved in the EPG process. Former members recounted that the newly appointed Indian ambassador to Nepal Sudhakar Dalela was the Joint Secretary (North) in the Ministry of External Affairs and was part of the EPG process during 2016-18. That apart, the new Nepali ambassador to India Nischal Nath Pandey also was part of the EPG process in Kathmandu.

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: A Russian nighttime attack on Zaporizhzhia in southern Ukraine has killed two civilians and wounded 48 others including four children

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A Russian nighttime attack on the southern Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia killed two civilians and wounded 48 others, including four children, officials said Tuesday (November 24, 2026), as authorities in Ukraine and Libya debated the legitimacy of an unprecedented Ukrainian strike on a Russian warship docked in Benghazi. The Zaporizhzhia glide bomb attack destroyed a private house and partially destroyed a five-story apartment building, according to Mykhailo Semikin, the head of the Zaporizhzhia Regional Military Administration. The youngest wounded child was less than a year old, he said, adding that the others were ages 4, 6 and 16. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Tuesday (November 24, 2026) that the Ukrainian military is sending reinforcements to the Zaporizhzhia region, which lies on the roughly 1,250-kilometer (almost 800-mile) front line snaking through eastern and southern Ukraine. Russia and Ukraine have escalated their aerial strikes in recent months even as they engage in U.S.-mediated talks to end the war that began with Moscow’s full-scale invasion of its neighbor nearly five years ago. Mr. Zelenskyy noted in a speech that Ukraine needs 115 billion euros ($126 billion) in aid from foreign countries next year to keep up the fight. Funding of 90 billion euros ($98.7 billion) is already assured, he said, but Ukraine needs to find another 25 billion euros ($27.4 billion). The United Nations says the war has killed close to 18,000 Ukrainian civilians and wounded more than 57,000 others since the all-out war broke out on Feb. 24, 2022. Hundreds of thousands of soldiers from both sides are believed to have died on the battlefield. Zelenskyy hails Ukraine's attack on a Russian warship in Libya Russia says four killed in major Ukraine drone barrage More than 700,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in the war, according to an estimate by independent Russian news outlets Meduza and Mediazona, which have been tracking Russian military losses for several years.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: They said that they received a huge dataset earlier this month that was hacked from Russia’s state statistics agency Rosstat by Belarusian activist group Cyber Partisans and a Ukrainian hacker group, Silent Crow. They added projected deaths not yet recorded by Russian authorities.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #21 of 30 (24 NOV)

📰 A Russian strike on Ukraine kills two, wounds 48 as Kyiv explains its attack in Libya

📌 Published: 24 Nov 2026, 10:44:46 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: A Russian nighttime attack on Zaporizhzhia in southern Ukraine has killed two civilians and wounded 48 others including four children

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A Russian nighttime attack on the southern Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia killed two civilians and wounded 48 others, including four children, officials said Tuesday (November 24, 2026), as authorities in Ukraine and Libya debated the legitimacy of an unprecedented Ukrainian strike on a Russian warship docked in Benghazi. The Zaporizhzhia glide bomb attack destroyed a private house and partially destroyed a five-story apartment building, according to Mykhailo Semikin, the head of the Zaporizhzhia Regional Military Administration. The youngest wounded child was less than a year old, he said, adding that the others were ages 4, 6 and 16. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Tuesday (November 24, 2026) that the Ukrainian military is sending reinforcements to the Zaporizhzhia region, which lies on the roughly 1,250-kilometer (almost 800-mile) front line snaking through eastern and southern Ukraine. Russia and Ukraine have escalated their aerial strikes in recent months even as they engage in U.S.-mediated talks to end the war that began with Moscow’s full-scale invasion of its neighbor nearly five years ago. Mr. Zelenskyy noted in a speech that Ukraine needs 115 billion euros ($126 billion) in aid from foreign countries next year to keep up the fight. Funding of 90 billion euros ($98.7 billion) is already assured, he said, but Ukraine needs to find another 25 billion euros ($27.4 billion). The United Nations says the war has killed close to 18,000 Ukrainian civilians and wounded more than 57,000 others since the all-out war broke out on Feb. 24, 2022. Hundreds of thousands of soldiers from both sides are believed to have died on the battlefield. Zelenskyy hails Ukraine's attack on a Russian warship in Libya Russia says four killed in major Ukraine drone barrage More than 700,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in the war, according to an estimate by independent Russian news outlets Meduza and Mediazona, which have been tracking Russian military losses for several years.

3. They added projected deaths not yet recorded by Russian authorities.

articles.title: Yemen officials say strike on buses, trucks kills 26
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Yemen, one of the world's poorest countries, has become the most active front in the West Asia war, with the Iran-backed Houthis and a Saudi-led coalition exchanging frequent attacks

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: An airstrike on trucks and buses killed 26 people in Yemen's southwest, local officials told AFP on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), as the Houthis and government forces traded blame for the attack. Yemen, one of the world's poorest countries, has become the most active front in the West Asia war, with the Iran-backed Houthis and a Saudi-led coalition exchanging frequent attacks. Two officials said coalition warplanes struck Houthi vehicles on Monday (November 23, 2026) in Lahj province, where the group has advanced in recent weeks towards Aden, the government's interim capital. The aircraft "targeted two vehicles belonging to the Houthis at the moment when a truck and a bus were passing by, in an area considered a front line", one of the officials said, adding 12 Houthi fighters and 14 civilians were killed. The second official confirmed the death toll. Witnesses reported seeing charred bodies at the scene. The Houthis' military spokesman blamed the Saudi air force for the strike, saying it would not go "unanswered". But government forces said the Houthis carried out the attack. The pro-Iran group targeted "civilian vehicles bearing no military markings, on a road that is a vital artery for the population", government forces spokesman Majed al-Nazli said. Separate strikes on Monday (November 23, 2026) killed 17 people and destroyed several buildings in the coastal province of Hodeida, the Houthis' telecommunications ministry said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Yemen, embroiled in more than a decade of civil war, was sucked into the wider U.S.-Iran conflict in July when a truce between the Houthis and the Saudi-backed government unravelled.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #22 of 30 (24 NOV)

📰 Yemen officials say strike on buses, trucks kills 26

📌 Published: 24 Nov 2026, 10:38:30 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Yemen, one of the world's poorest countries, has become the most active front in the West Asia war, with the Iran-backed Houthis and a Saudi-led coalition exchanging frequent attacks

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: An airstrike on trucks and buses killed 26 people in Yemen's southwest, local officials told AFP on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), as the Houthis and government forces traded blame for the attack. Yemen, one of the world's poorest countries, has become the most active front in the West Asia war, with the Iran-backed Houthis and a Saudi-led coalition exchanging frequent attacks. Two officials said coalition warplanes struck Houthi vehicles on Monday (November 23, 2026) in Lahj province, where the group has advanced in recent weeks towards Aden, the government's interim capital. The aircraft "targeted two vehicles belonging to the Houthis at the moment when a truck and a bus were passing by, in an area considered a front line", one of the officials said, adding 12 Houthi fighters and 14 civilians were killed. The second official confirmed the death toll. Witnesses reported seeing charred bodies at the scene. The Houthis' military spokesman blamed the Saudi air force for the strike, saying it would not go "unanswered". But government forces said the Houthis carried out the attack. The pro-Iran group targeted "civilian vehicles bearing no military markings, on a road that is a vital artery for the population", government forces spokesman Majed al-Nazli said. Separate strikes on Monday (November 23, 2026) killed 17 people and destroyed several buildings in the coastal province of Hodeida, the Houthis' telecommunications ministry said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Yemen, embroiled in more than a decade of civil war, was sucked into the wider U.S.-Iran conflict in July when a truce between the Houthis and the Saudi-backed government unravelled.

articles.title: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill seven including senior security official
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The ‌Israeli military and the Shin ‌Bet domestic ​security service said in ⁠a joint statement they ‌had struck a senior Hamas member, without identifying ‌him, adding ​that further details would ⁠be provided later

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Israeli airstrikes in Gaza on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) killed seven people including Hamas’s director of internal security, Palestinian officials and Israel said, despite a ceasefire in place since last year. Israel’s military said it “eliminated the terrorist Naim Muhammad Ashour Abu Nahal”, adding that he had been appointed to his post only two months ago but had been part of Hamas for a long time. “His elimination constitutes a blow to the apparatus’s management capabilities,” it said in a joint statement with Israel’s Shin Bet security agency. Israel’s caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defence Minister Israel Katz congratulated security forces, saying “no terrorist will escape the long arm” of their country. Mahmoud Bassal, spokesman for Gaza’s civil defence agency, which operates under Hamas authority, told AFP that several other people were in critical condition following the strike in Gaza City that killed Abu Nahal. The attack comes with talks underway in Israel to form a new government after October legislative elections produced no clear winner. Centrist Gadi Eisenkot is seeking to form a coalition to end Mr. Netanyahu’s long tenure. But Mr. Netanyahu, who has staked his reputation on ensuring security for Israel after the Hamas attack of October 7, 2023, remains in charge of military operations while negotiations continue. Mr. Bassal said earlier on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) that three people, including a 17-year-old, had been killed in a separate Israeli airstrike near Gaza City.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Three more were also killed in a third strike on a police station in the Al-Mawasi area in southern Gaza, he added.

hinglishTracks.en: Mahmoud Bassal, spokesman for Gaza’s civil defence agency, which operates under Hamas authority, told AFP that several other people were in critical condition following the strike in Gaza City that killed Abu Nahal.
