articles.title: Supreme Court bars Tamil Nadu government from coercive action against SASTRA University over land dispute
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: A Bench headed by CJI Surya Kant made absolute its interim order staying any coercive measures over 31.37 acres of government land allegedly encroached upon by the Thanjavur university

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Supreme Court on Monday (November 23, 2026) admitted an appeal filed by Shanmugha Arts Science Technology and Research Academy (SASTRA), a deemed university based in Thanjavur, against a Madras High Court direction to the Tamil Nadu government to evict it from 31.37 acres of public land in its occupation for nearly 40 years. The Court had already stayed the eviction of the university in an order passed on January 15, 2026, and had allowed the institution to carry out its activities without any hindrance. At that hearing, the Court asked the State government to consider three options of alternative lands offered by the university, instead of the land occupied and already utilised by it, represented by senior advocate Mukul Rohatgi. A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant had found the three options “just and fair”, and asked the State to consider the offer “sympathetically and take an appropriate decision by ensuring that no loss is caused to the public exchequer”. It also suggested that a high-powered committee of three senior officers of the State government accord a personal hearing to the university to “explain all the attending circumstances and also to persuade the authorities to accept one of the three options”. On August 10, 2026, the Court gave the State, represented by senior advocate Jaideep Gupta and Tamil Nadu Additional Advocate General Haripriya Padmanabhan, a “free hand in determining the actual market value of land” under dispute, with the university obligated to pay. The August order also recorded the university’s offer to pay the sale price of any land the State required for a public purpose, in this case the establishment of a prison, for which it wanted the disputed 31.37-acre property. The Court asked the State to take a “reasonably fair decision and apprise this court”. However, at the next hearing on September 21, 2026, the State sought more time to “consider the different options”. At the September 21 hearing, the Court noted that the land in dispute was used by an educational institution serving a public purpose, and asked why the State was so “obstinate” on eviction and demolition of the institution.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The State government had contended that the alternate parcels were inferior to the disputed land in terms of value, accessibility and contiguity, and that settling for alternative land could amount to putting a premium on encroachment.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #8 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Supreme Court bars Tamil Nadu government from coercive action against SASTRA University over land dispute

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 01:25:23 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: A Bench headed by CJI Surya Kant made absolute its interim order staying any coercive measures over 31.37 acres of government land allegedly encroached upon by the Thanjavur university

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Supreme Court on Monday (November 23, 2026) admitted an appeal filed by Shanmugha Arts Science Technology and Research Academy (SASTRA), a deemed university based in Thanjavur, against a Madras High Court direction to the Tamil Nadu government to evict it from 31.37 acres of public land in its occupation for nearly 40 years. The Court had already stayed the eviction of the university in an order passed on January 15, 2026, and had allowed the institution to carry out its activities without any hindrance. At that hearing, the Court asked the State government to consider three options of alternative lands offered by the university, instead of the land occupied and already utilised by it, represented by senior advocate Mukul Rohatgi. A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant had found the three options “just and fair”, and asked the State to consider the offer “sympathetically and take an appropriate decision by ensuring that no loss is caused to the public exchequer”. It also suggested that a high-powered committee of three senior officers of the State government accord a personal hearing to the university to “explain all the attending circumstances and also to persuade the authorities to accept one of the three options”. On August 10, 2026, the Court gave the State, represented by senior advocate Jaideep Gupta and Tamil Nadu Additional Advocate General Haripriya Padmanabhan, a “free hand in determining the actual market value of land” under dispute, with the university obligated to pay. The August order also recorded the university’s offer to pay the sale price of any land the State required for a public purpose, in this case the establishment of a prison, for which it wanted the disputed 31.37-acre property. The Court asked the State to take a “reasonably fair decision and apprise this court”. However, at the next hearing on September 21, 2026, the State sought more time to “consider the different options”. At the September 21 hearing, the Court noted that the land in dispute was used by an educational institution serving a public purpose, and asked why the State was so “obstinate” on eviction and demolition of the institution.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The State government had contended that the alternate parcels were inferior to the disputed land in terms of value, accessibility and contiguity, and that settling for alternative land could amount to putting a premium on encroachment.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Institutional (Adjective)
संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ।
✓ Syn: Systemic, Organizational, Constitutional  |  ✖ Ant: Individual, Informal, Unorganized
Establishment (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Establishment' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Accessibility (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Accessibility' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Encroachment (Adjective)
अतिक्रमण — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Encroachment' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Supreme Court bars Tamil Nadu government from coercive action against SASTRA University over land dispute", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. A Bench headed by CJI Surya Kant made absolute its interim order staying any coercive measures over 31.37 acres of government land allegedly...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Supreme Court bars Tamil Nadu government from co' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Supreme Court bars Tamil Nadu government from' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Supreme Court bars Tamil Nadu government from' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "A Bench headed by CJI Surya Kant made absolute its interim order staying any coercive measures over 31.37 acres of government land allegedly..." (Hinglish Arth: सीजेआई सूर्यकांत की अध्यक्षता वाली पीठ ने तंजावुर विश्वविद्यालय द्वारा कथित रूप से अतिक्रमण की गई 31.37 एकड़ सरकारी भूमि पर किसी भी कठोर कदम पर रोक लगाने के अपने अंतरिम आदेश को निरस्त कर दिया।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Supreme Court bars Tamil Nadu government from coercive action against SASTRA University over land dispute"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. The State government had contended that the alternate parcels were inferior to the disputed land in terms of value, accessibility and contiguity, and...
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "The State government had contended that the alternate parcels were inferior to the disputed land in terms of value, accessibility and contiguity, and..." (Hinglish Arth: राज्य सरकार ने तर्क दिया था कि वैकल्पिक भूखंड मूल्य, पहुंच और निकटता के मामले में विवादित भूमि से कमतर थे, और वैकल्पिक भूमि के लिए निपटान का मतलब उस पर प्रीमियम लगाना हो सकता है।)

articles.title: Supreme Court asks petitioner to move Allahabad High Court over ‘demolition’ of 100-year-old mosque at Saharanpur
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Declining to directly examine the allegations, the Supreme Court asked the petitioner to approach the jurisdictional High Court, saying that every alleged violation of a Supreme Court judgment cannot be brought directly before the apex court

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Supreme Court on Monday (November 23, 2026) declined to entertain a plea alleging that the demolition of a 100-year-old mosque in Uttar Pradesh's Saharanpur district violated the demolition guidelines laid down by it in a landmark 2024 judgment on the use of bulldozers . A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana was hearing a plea filed by Imran Ahmad against Uttar Pradesh Chief Secretary Shashi Prakash Goyal, alleging non-compliance with the apex court's directions. Declining to undertake a direct examination of the allegations, the Bench asked the petitioner to approach the jurisdictional High Court, saying that every alleged violation of a Supreme Court judgment cannot be brought directly before the apex court. "Every order violating a Supreme Court judgment cannot come back to the Supreme Court itself. You have to go to the respective high court," CJI said. The Bench said determining whether the demolition guidelines had been violated would require an examination of the specific facts and circumstances surrounding the alleged demolition, a task more appropriately undertaken by the jurisdictional High Court. "We have laid down the principles, but then wherever these principles have been violated, in what factual context and background? Please go to the concerned high court, establish your case on facts, and if the high court doesn't grant you necessary relief, then come to us," the CJI said. The Bench further clarified that it could not undertake a factual inquiry into the allegations in the contempt proceedings. ALSO WATCH Watch: How the Supreme Court clamped down on ‘bulldozer’ demolitions | Explained However, the Bench made it clear that if the High Court, upon examining the matter, finds that the Supreme Court's directions have been violated, appropriate consequences would follow.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The petitioner was asked to approach the jurisdictional High Court and seek appropriate relief.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #9 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Supreme Court asks petitioner to move Allahabad High Court over ‘demolition’ of 100-year-old mosque at Saharanpur

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 01:20:27 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Declining to directly examine the allegations, the Supreme Court asked the petitioner to approach the jurisdictional High Court, saying that every alleged violation of a Supreme Court judgment cannot be brought directly before the apex court

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Supreme Court on Monday (November 23, 2026) declined to entertain a plea alleging that the demolition of a 100-year-old mosque in Uttar Pradesh's Saharanpur district violated the demolition guidelines laid down by it in a landmark 2024 judgment on the use of bulldozers . A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana was hearing a plea filed by Imran Ahmad against Uttar Pradesh Chief Secretary Shashi Prakash Goyal, alleging non-compliance with the apex court's directions. Declining to undertake a direct examination of the allegations, the Bench asked the petitioner to approach the jurisdictional High Court, saying that every alleged violation of a Supreme Court judgment cannot be brought directly before the apex court. "Every order violating a Supreme Court judgment cannot come back to the Supreme Court itself. You have to go to the respective high court," CJI said. The Bench said determining whether the demolition guidelines had been violated would require an examination of the specific facts and circumstances surrounding the alleged demolition, a task more appropriately undertaken by the jurisdictional High Court. "We have laid down the principles, but then wherever these principles have been violated, in what factual context and background? Please go to the concerned high court, establish your case on facts, and if the high court doesn't grant you necessary relief, then come to us," the CJI said. The Bench further clarified that it could not undertake a factual inquiry into the allegations in the contempt proceedings. ALSO WATCH Watch: How the Supreme Court clamped down on ‘bulldozer’ demolitions | Explained However, the Bench made it clear that if the High Court, upon examining the matter, finds that the Supreme Court's directions have been violated, appropriate consequences would follow.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The petitioner was asked to approach the jurisdictional High Court and seek appropriate relief.

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: Declining to directly examine the allegations, the Supreme Court asked the petitioner to approach the jurisdictional High Court, saying that every alleged violation of a Supreme Court judgment cannot be brought directly before the apex court
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Supreme Court on Monday (November 23, 2026) declined to entertain a plea alleging that the demolition of a 100-year-old mosque in Uttar Pradesh's Saharanpur district violated the demolition guidelines laid down by it in a landmark 2024 judgment on the use of bulldozers . A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana was hearing a plea filed by Imran Ahmad against Uttar Pradesh Chief Secretary Shashi Prakash Goyal, alleging non-compliance with the apex court's directions. Declining to undertake a direct examination of the allegations, the Bench asked the petitioner to approach the jurisdictional High Court, saying that every alleged violation of a Supreme Court judgment cannot be brought directly before the apex court. "Every order violating a Supreme Court judgment cannot come back to the Supreme Court itself. You have to go to the respective high court," CJI said. The Bench said determining whether the demolition guidelines had been violated would require an examination of the specific facts and circumstances surrounding the alleged demolition, a task more appropriately undertaken by the jurisdictional High Court. "We have laid down the principles, but then wherever these principles have been violated, in what factual context and background? Please go to the concerned high court, establish your case on facts, and if the high court doesn't grant you necessary relief, then come to us," the CJI said. The Bench further clarified that it could not undertake a factual inquiry into the allegations in the contempt proceedings. ALSO WATCH Watch: How the Supreme Court clamped down on ‘bulldozer’ demolitions | Explained However, the Bench made it clear that if the High Court, upon examining the matter, finds that the Supreme Court's directions have been violated, appropriate consequences would follow.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The petitioner was asked to approach the jurisdictional High Court and seek appropriate relief.

articles.title: Earthmover at Amarnath Yatra stopover Sheshnag lake draws outrage from parties and locals

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Demands are growing to stop such heavy machines in the ecologically fragile region

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A viral video of an earthmover operating at Sheshnag — the high-altitude and inaccessible glacial lake located 11,780 feet above sea level in south Kashmir’s Pahalgam — evoked outrage from political parties and locals on Monday (November 23). Demands are growing to stop such heavy machines in the ecologically fragile region. The undated video shows an earthmover filling a site at the lake's edge, which spans 1.1 kilometres in length and 0.7 kilometres in width. Sheshnag is a stopover for pilgrims heading to the annual Amarnath Yatra in south Kashmir’s Anantnag. A macadamised road for the pilgrims ends at Chandanwari. In the past, pilgrims trekked 12 to 13 kilometres on an unpaved mountain track to reach the lake. The Amarnath cave is 18-20 km from the stopover. Opposition People’s Democratic Party (PDP) spokesman Mohit Bhan said Sheshnag was not just another lake in the mountains of Kashmir. “In Hinduism, it is the sacred landscape where Lord Shiva is believed to have left behind the serpents before proceeding towards the Amarnath Cave to narrate the Amar Katha to Goddess Parvati. There is a profound contradiction in invoking Hindu faith while allowing the very landscape associated with that faith to be disturbed through unnecessary construction, road cutting and surface levelling,” said Mr. Bhan. The visuals and reports of heavy machinery operating near the pristine Sheshnag Lake, in the glacial zone of Pahalgam are very disturbing, raising serious concern among people about the ecological impact of construction in this fragile Himalayan region. With our glaciers already retreating, and recent devastating glacier-related floods in neighbouring Nepal reminding us of the growing vulnerability of the Himalayas, such activities raise alarm. Kashmir has always warmly welcomed Amarnath Yatra pilgrims, and improving facilities for them has never been an issue. But not at the cost of our fragile ecosystem. Those governing owe answers to people for the serious environmental concerns created by such "developmental projects"! Our precious mountains, glaciers and water bodies need protection not plunder, for now and for the future generations. So this must be immediately stopped. He said what is being projected as development must not come at the cost of a fragile alpine ecosystem and a landscape deeply embedded in Hindu religious belief. “Faith and ecology are not competing interests. Both demand protection. You cannot celebrate the sanctity of a pilgrimage while disregarding the sanctity of the landscape through which it passes. If we cannot respect Sacred Sheshnag, what exactly are we preserving in the name of the Amarnath Yatra?” he said. Kashmir’s chief cleric Mirwaiz Umar Farooq said the visuals and reports of heavy machinery operating near the pristine lake, in the glacial zone of Pahalgam, were “very disturbing”, “raising serious concern among people about the ecological impact of construction in this fragile Himalayan region”. “With our glaciers already retreating, and recent devastating glacier-related floods in neighbouring Nepal reminding us of the growing vulnerability of the Himalayas, such activities raise alarm. Kashmir has always warmly welcomed Amarnath Yatra pilgrims, and improving facilities for them has never been an issue. But not at the cost of our fragile ecosystem. Those governing owe answers to people for the serious environmental concerns created by such ‘developmental projects’! Our precious mountains, glaciers and water bodies need protection, not plunder, for now and for future generations. So, this must be immediately stopped,” said the Mirwaiz. Many commented on the video, which went viral on social media platforms in the past 24 hours. “Sheshnag Lake is one of the 14 officially identified high-risk glacial lakes in J&K for GLOF (glacial lake outburst flood). Heavy machinery is being run on its shoreline with zero transparency on environmental clearance or risk assessment. This is not development. This is deliberate endangerment of a fragile alpine ecosystem and downstream communities,” said Suhail Ahmed Khan, from Kashmir.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Raja Muzaffar Bhat, a prominent environmentalist and activist, termed the earthmover at the high-altitude lake a “disaster”. “How does such a heavy machine reach our glaciers of Kashmir?” he asked.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #10 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Earthmover at Amarnath Yatra stopover Sheshnag lake draws outrage from parties and locals

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 01:17:32 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Demands are growing to stop such heavy machines in the ecologically fragile region

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A viral video of an earthmover operating at Sheshnag — the high-altitude and inaccessible glacial lake located 11,780 feet above sea level in south Kashmir’s Pahalgam — evoked outrage from political parties and locals on Monday (November 23). Demands are growing to stop such heavy machines in the ecologically fragile region. The undated video shows an earthmover filling a site at the lake's edge, which spans 1.1 kilometres in length and 0.7 kilometres in width. Sheshnag is a stopover for pilgrims heading to the annual Amarnath Yatra in south Kashmir’s Anantnag. A macadamised road for the pilgrims ends at Chandanwari. In the past, pilgrims trekked 12 to 13 kilometres on an unpaved mountain track to reach the lake. The Amarnath cave is 18-20 km from the stopover. Opposition People’s Democratic Party (PDP) spokesman Mohit Bhan said Sheshnag was not just another lake in the mountains of Kashmir. “In Hinduism, it is the sacred landscape where Lord Shiva is believed to have left behind the serpents before proceeding towards the Amarnath Cave to narrate the Amar Katha to Goddess Parvati. There is a profound contradiction in invoking Hindu faith while allowing the very landscape associated with that faith to be disturbed through unnecessary construction, road cutting and surface levelling,” said Mr. Bhan. The visuals and reports of heavy machinery operating near the pristine Sheshnag Lake, in the glacial zone of Pahalgam are very disturbing, raising serious concern among people about the ecological impact of construction in this fragile Himalayan region. With our glaciers already retreating, and recent devastating glacier-related floods in neighbouring Nepal reminding us of the growing vulnerability of the Himalayas, such activities raise alarm. articles.title: TMC MLA Sabina Yeasmin appears before NIA in connection with ‘attacks’ on judicial officers
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The NIA has been probing the alleged attacks on judicial officers and a judge's vehicle during violence in the Kaliachak and Mothabari areas on April 1

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: TMC MLA Sabina Yeasmin and her husband appeared before the National Investigation Agency (NIA) on Monday (November 23, 2026) in connection with its investigation into alleged attacks on judicial magistrates during the SIR exercise in West Bengal's Malda district. The NIA has been probing the alleged attacks on judicial officers and a judge's vehicle during violence in the Kaliachak and Mothabari areas on April 1. Demonstrators had blocked National Highway 12 at Kaliachak to protest against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Ms. Yeasmin, along with her husband Mehebub Alam, appeared before NIA officials at the agency's New Town office and claimed that they had no knowledge of the alleged attacks and violence on April 1 and that they were not present at the site. "This is a politically motivated move," she told reporters before entering the NIA office. Ms. Yeasmin claimed that her husband was at the collector's office regarding her nomination papers, which were to be filed the next day (on April 2) for the assembly elections, when the violence occurred. She won the Sujapur seat in the assembly polls this year. The MLA said she was at the BDO office, staging a demonstration along with some party supporters. "Neither my husband nor I had any role in the road blockade," she said. Ms. Yeasmin had joined the Ritabrata Banerjee-led faction of Trinamool Congress, following the West Bengal assembly elections, which the BJP won.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Later, she resigned from her post as president of the Democratic Trinamool Congress women’s wing in October and expressed her personal allegiance to former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee.

hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — बाद में, उन्होंने अक्टूबर में डेमोक्रेटिक तृणमूल कांग्रेस महिला विंग के अध्यक्ष पद से इस्तीफा दे दिया और पश्चिम बंगाल की पूर्व मुख्यमंत्री ममता बनर्जी के प्रति अपनी व्यक्तिगत निष्ठा व्यक्त की।।

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #11 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 TMC MLA Sabina Yeasmin appears before NIA in connection with ‘attacks’ on judicial officers

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 01:16:00 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The NIA has been probing the alleged attacks on judicial officers and a judge's vehicle during violence in the Kaliachak and Mothabari areas on April 1

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: TMC MLA Sabina Yeasmin and her husband appeared before the National Investigation Agency (NIA) on Monday (November 23, 2026) in connection with its investigation into alleged attacks on judicial magistrates during the SIR exercise in West Bengal's Malda district. The NIA has been probing the alleged attacks on judicial officers and a judge's vehicle during violence in the Kaliachak and Mothabari areas on April 1. Demonstrators had blocked National Highway 12 at Kaliachak to protest against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Ms. Yeasmin, along with her husband Mehebub Alam, appeared before NIA officials at the agency's New Town office and claimed that they had no knowledge of the alleged attacks and violence on April 1 and that they were not present at the site. "This is a politically motivated move," she told reporters before entering the NIA office. Ms. Yeasmin claimed that her husband was at the collector's office regarding her nomination papers, which were to be filed the next day (on April 2) for the assembly elections, when the violence occurred. She won the Sujapur seat in the assembly polls this year. The MLA said she was at the BDO office, staging a demonstration along with some party supporters. "Neither my husband nor I had any role in the road blockade," she said. Ms. Yeasmin had joined the Ritabrata Banerjee-led faction of Trinamool Congress, following the West Bengal assembly elections, which the BJP won.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Later, she resigned from her post as president of the Democratic Trinamool Congress women’s wing in October and expressed her personal allegiance to former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee.

articles.title: Rahul Gandhi’s Gaza remarks expose old fault lines between Congress and Left

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The backlash from Left parties to the Congress leader’s comments on Israel and Gaza underscores enduring ideological differences within the Opposition alliance

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The recent remarks of Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi hyphenating the October 7 Hamas attack on Israel with the deaths of tens of thousands of Palestinians in Gaza have triggered a sharp backlash from Left parties, exposing ideological fault lines within the Indian National Developmental, Inclusive Alliance. The controversy has highlighted the distance that continues to separate the Congress and the Left on questions of international politics, despite their present-day electoral cooperation. The disagreement echoes earlier tensions that culminated in the Left withdrawing support to the United Progressive Alliance government over the India-U.S. nuclear deal in 2008. The CPI(M) had walked out of the alliance, denouncing what it described as the Indian government’s subservient position to the U.S. While the current dispute is unlikely to threaten the alliance in the immediate future, it is a reminder that Opposition unity often coexists with significant ideological divergence. Within the Congress , some leaders privately view the episode as a correction to what they saw as the party leadership’s growing proximity to sections of the Left. A senior Congress leader argued that the controversy is unlikely to have significant political consequences for the party, noting that Palestine is no longer a mass political issue in India beyond activist circles and sections of campuses. The leadership expects the storm to subside as public attention shifts elsewhere. The controversy stems from remarks made by Mr. Gandhi during an interaction at the University of Chicago last week. Responding to a question on foreign policy, he said: “India’s foreign policy must be guided by what is good for India… I support a strong relationship with Israel. We have strategic interests, including buying the best weapons for our armed forces.”
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: India / Palestine / Israel-Palestine Conflict / Israel / Rahul Gandhi / politics / government / Analysis

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #12 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Rahul Gandhi’s Gaza remarks expose old fault lines between Congress and Left

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 01:15:47 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The backlash from Left parties to the Congress leader’s comments on Israel and Gaza underscores enduring ideological differences within the Opposition alliance

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The recent remarks of Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi hyphenating the October 7 Hamas attack on Israel with the deaths of tens of thousands of Palestinians in Gaza have triggered a sharp backlash from Left parties, exposing ideological fault lines within the Indian National Developmental, Inclusive Alliance. The controversy has highlighted the distance that continues to separate the Congress and the Left on questions of international politics, despite their present-day electoral cooperation. The disagreement echoes earlier tensions that culminated in the Left withdrawing support to the United Progressive Alliance government over the India-U.S. nuclear deal in 2008. The CPI(M) had walked out of the alliance, denouncing what it described as the Indian government’s subservient position to the U.S. While the current dispute is unlikely to threaten the alliance in the immediate future, it is a reminder that Opposition unity often coexists with significant ideological divergence. Within the Congress , some leaders privately view the episode as a correction to what they saw as the party leadership’s growing proximity to sections of the Left. A senior Congress leader argued that the controversy is unlikely to have significant political consequences for the party, noting that Palestine is no longer a mass political issue in India beyond activist circles and sections of campuses. The leadership expects the storm to subside as public attention shifts elsewhere. The controversy stems from remarks made by Mr. Gandhi during an interaction at the University of Chicago last week. Responding to a question on foreign policy, he said: “India’s foreign policy must be guided by what is good for India… I support a strong relationship with Israel. We have strategic interests, including buying the best weapons for our armed forces.”

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: India / Palestine / Israel-Palestine Conflict / Israel / Rahul Gandhi / politics / government / Analysis

articles.title: Ukraine says Russian strikes kill 15 in Kyiv region
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Moscow has been pummelling Ukraine with nightly aerial barrages as the war-torn country braces for another winter, as the full-scale invasion grinds through its fifth year

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Rescuers in Ukraine raced on Monday (November 23, 2026) to find residents trapped under the rubble of a block of flats that partially collapsed in a Russian strike, a fter attacks on the Kyiv region killed at least 15 people. Moscow has been pummelling Ukraine with nightly aerial barrages as the war-torn country braces for another winter, as the full-scale invasion grinds through its fifth year. Russian President Vladimir Putin vowed last week a "painful" response to Ukrainian strikes on Russia's Crimea bridge after holding a summit with U.S. counterpart Donald Trump and China's Xi Jinping. An overnight strike on Dymer, around 45 kilometres (30 miles) north of the Ukrainian capital, hit a five-storey building, killing at least 11 people, according to Kyiv regional official Tymur Tkachenko. AFP images showed rescuers combing through the mound of smouldering rubble. "Rescuers recovered the body of another person from beneath the rubble," Tkachenko wrote on Telegram, confirming the death toll had risen to 11. Ukraine's State Emergency Service said earlier on Telegram that the dead included a teenager and a woman in her forties. It said earlier that rescuers were searching for 11 people, including two children, who were "not responding or cannot be reached". Rescuers had managed to pull out people from the rubble including a 79-year-old woman and a child, Tkachenko said.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Ukrainian human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets called the attack part of "Russia's genocidal war against Ukraine".

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #19 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Ukraine says Russian strikes kill 15 in Kyiv region

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 12:02:17 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Moscow has been pummelling Ukraine with nightly aerial barrages as the war-torn country braces for another winter, as the full-scale invasion grinds through its fifth year

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Rescuers in Ukraine raced on Monday (November 23, 2026) to find residents trapped under the rubble of a block of flats that partially collapsed in a Russian strike, a fter attacks on the Kyiv region killed at least 15 people. Moscow has been pummelling Ukraine with nightly aerial barrages as the war-torn country braces for another winter, as the full-scale invasion grinds through its fifth year. Russian President Vladimir Putin vowed last week a "painful" response to Ukrainian strikes on Russia's Crimea bridge after holding a summit with U.S. counterpart Donald Trump and China's Xi Jinping. An overnight strike on Dymer, around 45 kilometres (30 miles) north of the Ukrainian capital, hit a five-storey building, killing at least 11 people, according to Kyiv regional official Tymur Tkachenko. AFP images showed rescuers combing through the mound of smouldering rubble. "Rescuers recovered the body of another person from beneath the rubble," Tkachenko wrote on Telegram, confirming the death toll had risen to 11. Ukraine's State Emergency Service said earlier on Telegram that the dead included a teenager and a woman in her forties. It said earlier that rescuers were searching for 11 people, including two children, who were "not responding or cannot be reached". Rescuers had managed to pull out people from the rubble including a 79-year-old woman and a child, Tkachenko said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Ukrainian human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets called the attack part of "Russia's genocidal war against Ukraine".

articles.title: Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif to undertake official visit to Russia
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The three-day visit to Russia will begin on November 30, aiming to strengthen bilateral ties by securing energy and investment agreements

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif is set to undertake his first official visit to Russia, followed by a trip to Iran for a regional summit. The three-day visit to Russia will begin on November 30, aiming to strengthen bilateral ties by securing energy and investment agreements, reported Dawn . During his meeting with Russian President Vladi­mir Putin, discussions are expected to focus on ene­rgy cooperation, defence, trade, regional security and investment, a source in the Prime Minister’s Office told Dawn. The revival of Pakistan Steel Mills, established with Russian assistance, is also likely to feature prominently, alongside potential Russian investment in Pakistan’s oil and gas sectors. The two countries are likely to examine possibilities for Russian cooperation in restoring the industrial facility, alongside broader initiatives aimed at supporting Pakistan’s industrial development. Later, Prime Minister Shehbaz will be travelling to Iran for the 18th Economic Coo­peration Organisation (ECO) Summit from December 3-4, according to Dawn . Leaders of 10 member States will discuss regional trade, connectivity, energy, transportation, investment and industrial cooperation.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The summit comes ahead of Pakistan assuming the ECO chairmanship for 2026-27.

hinglishTracks.en: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif is set to undertake his first official visit to Russia, followed by a trip to Iran for a regional summit.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — प्रधान मंत्री शहबाज़ शरीफ़ रूस की अपनी पहली आधिकारिक यात्रा करने के लिए तैयार हैं, जिसके बाद एक क्षेत्रीय शिखर सम्मेलन के लिए ईरान की यात्रा होगी।।

hinglishTracks.en: The summit comes ahead of Pakistan assuming the ECO chairmanship for 2026-27.

📰 Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif to undertake official visit to Russia

🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The three-day visit to Russia will begin on November 30, aiming to strengthen bilateral ties by securing energy and investment agreements

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif is set to undertake his first official visit to Russia, followed by a trip to Iran for a regional summit. The three-day visit to Russia will begin on November 30, aiming to strengthen bilateral ties by securing energy and investment agreements, reported Dawn . During his meeting with Russian President Vladi­mir Putin, discussions are expected to focus on ene­rgy cooperation, defence, trade, regional security and investment, a source in the Prime Minister’s Office told Dawn. The revival of Pakistan Steel Mills, established with Russian assistance, is also likely to feature prominently, alongside potential Russian investment in Pakistan’s oil and gas sectors. The two countries are likely to examine possibilities for Russian cooperation in restoring the industrial facility, alongside broader initiatives aimed at supporting Pakistan’s industrial development. Later, Prime Minister Shehbaz will be travelling to Iran for the 18th Economic Coo­peration Organisation (ECO) Summit from December 3-4, according to Dawn . Leaders of 10 member States will discuss regional trade, connectivity, energy, transportation, investment and industrial cooperation.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The summit comes ahead of Pakistan assuming the ECO chairmanship for 2026-27.

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: While there is no single magic number of minutes that is just the right amount of time to sit on the toilet, the broad agreement is up to 5 minutes. Scrolling your phone while sitting for long stretches of time may increase your risk of haemorrhoids

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Every time I called my cousin Arun* around 9 a.m., his voice would echo, as though he were in a bathroom. “I’m on the throne, I’ll call you in 20 minutes,” he would say. The first time I heard this, it took me a while to understand what ‘the throne’ was, and as if that was not confusing enough, what was he doing there for 20 minutes. Perplexed, I asked him why he had the phone in the bathroom when he was doing his morning business, to which he casually replied that he would sit on the throne solving Wordle, crosswords and reading the news until he ‘downloaded’. A couple of months ago he told me that he was diagnosed with early stages of haemorrhoids and was on treatment. I advised him on this matter, stressing how his morning ritual could be contributing to his condition. This ultimately led to his ‘conscious reduction of phone time in the bathroom’. His words, not mine. Recently, he proudly announced that his scheduled ‘throne time’ was now down to six minutes, every morning after breakfast. Bathroom humour is universal. Cinema is no exception — it has found humour and dependable plotlines from this predictable ritual. Just one instance is in Lokesh Kanagaraj’s Vikram , where a character pulling the flush coincides with the house exploding. Thankfully, the consequences of spending 20 minutes on the toilet are far less dramatic.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: health / Gastroenterology / gastrointestinal disease

hinglishTracks.en: While there is no single magic number of minutes that is just the right amount of time to sit on the toilet, the broad agreement is up to 5 minutes.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — हालाँकि मिनटों की कोई एक जादुई संख्या नहीं है जो शौचालय पर बैठने के लिए सही समय हो, व्यापक सहमति 5 मिनट तक है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Agreement' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: समझौता — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Agreement' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: Scrolling your phone while sitting for long stretches of time may increase your risk of haemorrhoids
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — लंबे समय तक बैठकर फोन स्क्रॉल करने से बवासीर का खतरा बढ़ सकता है।

hinglishTracks.en: Every time I called my cousin Arun* around 9 a.m., his voice would echo, as though he were in a bathroom.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — जब भी मैं सुबह 9 बजे के आसपास अपने चचेरे भाई अरुण* को फोन करता था, तो उसकी आवाज गूंजती थी, जैसे कि वह बाथरूम में हो।।

hinglishTracks.en: “I’m on the throne, I’ll call you in 20 minutes,” he would say.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — वह कहते थे, ''मैं सिंहासन पर हूं, मैं आपको 20 मिनट में फोन करूंगा।''।

hinglishTracks.en: The first time I heard this, it took me a while to understand what ‘the throne’ was, and as if that was not confusing enough, what was he doing there for 20 minutes.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — पहली बार जब मैंने इसे सुना, तो मुझे यह समझने में थोड़ा समय लगा कि 'सिंहासन' क्या है, और जैसे कि यह इतना भ्रमित करने वाला नहीं था कि वह 20 मिनट तक वहां क्या कर रहा था।।

hinglishTracks.en: Perplexed, I asked him why he had the phone in the bathroom when he was doing his morning business, to which he casually replied that he would sit on the throne solving Wordle, crosswords and reading the news until he ‘downloaded’.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — हैरान होकर, मैंने उससे पूछा कि जब वह अपना सुबह का काम कर रहा था तो उसके पास बाथरूम में फोन क्यों था, जिस पर उसने लापरवाही से जवाब दिया कि वह सिंहासन पर बैठकर वर्डले, क्रॉसवर्ड हल करेगा और समाचार तब तक पढ़ेगा जब तक वह 'डाउनलोड' नहीं कर लेता।।

hinglishTracks.en: A couple of months ago he told me that he was diagnosed with early stages of haemorrhoids and was on treatment.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — कुछ महीने पहले उन्होंने मुझे बताया था कि उन्हें बवासीर की प्रारंभिक अवस्था का पता चला है और उनका इलाज चल रहा है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Treatment' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: इलाज — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Treatment' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: I advised him on this matter, stressing how his morning ritual could be contributing to his condition.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — मैंने उसे इस मामले पर सलाह दी, इस बात पर जोर देते हुए कि उसकी सुबह की रस्म उसकी स्थिति में कैसे योगदान दे सकती है।।

hinglishTracks.en: This ultimately led to his ‘conscious reduction of phone time in the bathroom’.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — इससे अंततः उन्हें 'बाथरूम में फोन के समय में सचेत कमी' आई।।

hinglishTracks.en: His words, not mine.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — उसके शब्द, मेरे नहीं.।

hinglishTracks.en: Recently, he proudly announced that his scheduled ‘throne time’ was now down to six minutes, every morning after breakfast.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — हाल ही में, उन्होंने गर्व से घोषणा की कि उनका निर्धारित 'सिंहासन समय' अब हर सुबह नाश्ते के बाद छह मिनट तक कम हो गया है।।

hinglishTracks.en: Bathroom humour is universal.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — बाथरूम का हास्य सार्वभौमिक है।।

hinglishTracks.en: Cinema is no exception — it has found humour and dependable plotlines from this predictable ritual.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — सिनेमा कोई अपवाद नहीं है - इसने इस पूर्वानुमेय अनुष्ठान से हास्य और भरोसेमंद कथानक पाया है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Predictably' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: जैसा पहले से अनुमान था — बिना किसी आश्चर्य के बिल्कुल पूर्वानुमान के मुताबिक होना। इसके Synonyms हैं: Foreseeably, Expectedly, Inevitably और Antonyms हैं: Unexpectedly, Surprisingly, Abruptly।

hinglishTracks.en: Just one instance is in Lokesh Kanagaraj’s Vikram , where a character pulling the flush coincides with the house exploding.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — केवल एक उदाहरण लोकेश कनगराज की विक्रम में है, जहां एक पात्र फ्लश खींच रहा है और घर में विस्फोट हो रहा है।।

hinglishTracks.en: Thankfully, the consequences of spending 20 minutes on the toilet are far less dramatic.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — शुक्र है, शौचालय में 20 मिनट बिताने के परिणाम बहुत कम नाटकीय हैं।।

hinglishTracks.en: health / Gastroenterology / gastrointestinal disease
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — स्वास्थ्य / गैस्ट्रोएंटरोलॉजी / गैस्ट्रोइंटेस्टाइनल रोग। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Gastrointestinal' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: गैस्ट्रोइंटेस्टाइनल — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Gastrointestinal' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #29 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 How long is too long on the throne?

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 01:35:56 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: While there is no single magic number of minutes that is just the right amount of time to sit on the toilet, the broad agreement is up to 5 minutes. Scrolling your phone while sitting for long stretches of time may increase your risk of haemorrhoids

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Every time I called my cousin Arun* around 9 a.m., his voice would echo, as though he were in a bathroom. “I’m on the throne, I’ll call you in 20 minutes,” he would say. The first time I heard this, it took me a while to understand what ‘the throne’ was, and as if that was not confusing enough, what was he doing there for 20 minutes. Perplexed, I asked him why he had the phone in the bathroom when he was doing his morning business, to which he casually replied that he would sit on the throne solving Wordle, crosswords and reading the news until he ‘downloaded’. A couple of months ago he told me that he was diagnosed with early stages of haemorrhoids and was on treatment. I advised him on this matter, stressing how his morning ritual could be contributing to his condition. This ultimately led to his ‘conscious reduction of phone time in the bathroom’. His words, not mine. Recently, he proudly announced that his scheduled ‘throne time’ was now down to six minutes, every morning after breakfast. Bathroom humour is universal. Cinema is no exception — it has found humour and dependable plotlines from this predictable ritual. Just one instance is in Lokesh Kanagaraj’s Vikram , where a character pulling the flush coincides with the house exploding. Thankfully, the consequences of spending 20 minutes on the toilet are far less dramatic.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: health / Gastroenterology / gastrointestinal disease

articles.title: India’s recurring pollution crisis calls for a sustained movement for cleaner air
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: India’s fight against air pollution requires public engagement, effective communication and changes in civic behaviour; lessons from Swachh Bharat Mission offer a template for mobilising citizens to take ownership of clean air through collective action and responsible habits

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: D eepavali, the festival of lights, left a trail of dark smoke across large parts of India’s northern plains, especially around the national capital, Delhi, where 80 million people, particularly infants and the elderly, are struggling to breathe. The Air Quality Index (AQI) at several locations in the National Capital Region (NCR) had touched 400, indicating the severity of the conditions. Other cities and towns in the north, south, east and west, though better off than the NCR because of favourable weather and geographical advantages, do not have pristine air either. Air in most Indian cities contains pollutants, including particulate matter, at levels about eight times higher than the threshold set by the World Health Organization. The worst part of the problem is its dire predictability, except for concessions from the weather. The costly lessons from the capital have implications for the entire country. The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) swiftly moved up the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) from Stage I to Stage III within 15 days. The Commission, a statutory body established as an emergency response to toxic air conditions, has been cracking down on farm fires in Punjab, with its teams visiting fields to check incidents of stubble burning. PAVAN-I3C, the CAQM’s new Integrated Command and Control Centre, seeks to capture non-compliance in industries, traffic and transport systems and trigger immediate action against pollution spikes. Construction and demolition (C&D) activities have been halted until the 20th of this month. Inspections of construction sites and checks of Pollution Under Control Certificates (PUCC) are also vigorous. Last week, in an unprecedented move, CAQM directed Delhi and other NCR States to plan reduction of annual pollution levels by 15-20% forthwith. Regulatory moves, however essential, are not enough. Fines and work stoppages offer only partial deterrence, while obstructions and congestion on roads are an outright failure of enforcement. Institutional compliance, enforcement and monitoring by agencies are paramount, but civic behaviour is equally critical. The asks of people are not any great sacrifices, but some lifestyle retuning: use public transport and minimise use of personal vehicles, work from home, avoid construction activities for a few weeks, clean air filters at homes and in vehicles, avoid activities which generate dust, heat and smoke, and avoid open burning of solid waste and biomass. It would be unimaginable in many other countries for vehicle owners to be reminded of the pollution caused by their vehicles only during the months when the air becomes unbreathable. If clean air is part of the right to life, citizens also have a charter of duties to follow. The causes of pollution are well known. These straddle sectors, including industry, roads and buildings, vehicles, agriculture, shrinking green cover, municipal waste and urban living. However, citizens and their behaviour, in their varied roles as farmers, car and house owners, builders, contractors, and urban residents, remain at the centre. People complain and curse, and even silently suffer sickness from foul air, but sensitive and responsive behaviour remains elusive. The expansion of metro services and the availability of more public transport have not persuaded private car owners to switch. The Supreme Court went the extra mile by allowing firecrackers this Deepavali, while imposing justifiable restrictions on their toxic content and duration of use. articles.deepExplanation:
1. Core Context & Background: India’s fight against air pollution requires public engagement, effective communication and changes in civic behaviour; lessons from Swachh Bharat Mission offer a template for mobilising citizens to take ownership of clean air through collective action and responsible habits

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: D eepavali, the festival of lights, left a trail of dark smoke across large parts of India’s northern plains, especially around the national capital, Delhi, where 80 million people, particularly infants and the elderly, are struggling to breathe. The Air Quality Index (AQI) at several locations in the National Capital Region (NCR) had touched 400, indicating the severity of the conditions. Other cities and towns in the north, south, east and west, though better off than the NCR because of favourable weather and geographical advantages, do not have pristine air either. Air in most Indian cities contains pollutants, including particulate matter, at levels about eight times higher than the threshold set by the World Health Organization. The worst part of the problem is its dire predictability, except for concessions from the weather. The costly lessons from the capital have implications for the entire country. The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) swiftly moved up the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) from Stage I to Stage III within 15 days. The Commission, a statutory body established as an emergency response to toxic air conditions, has been cracking down on farm fires in Punjab, with its teams visiting fields to check incidents of stubble burning. PAVAN-I3C, the CAQM’s new Integrated Command and Control Centre, seeks to capture non-compliance in industries, traffic and transport systems and trigger immediate action against pollution spikes. Construction and demolition (C&D) activities have been halted until the 20th of this month. Inspections of construction sites and checks of Pollution Under Control Certificates (PUCC) are also vigorous. Last week, in an unprecedented move, CAQM directed Delhi and other NCR States to plan reduction of annual pollution levels by 15-20% forthwith. Regulatory moves, however essential, are not enough. Fines and work stoppages offer only partial deterrence, while obstructions and congestion on roads are an outright failure of enforcement. Institutional compliance, enforcement and monitoring by agencies are paramount, but civic behaviour is equally critical. The asks of people are not any great sacrifices, but some lifestyle retuning: use public transport and minimise use of personal vehicles, work from home, avoid construction activities for a few weeks, clean air filters at homes and in vehicles, avoid activities which generate dust, heat and smoke, and avoid open burning of solid waste and biomass. It would be unimaginable in many other countries for vehicle owners to be reminded of the pollution caused by their vehicles only during the months when the air becomes unbreathable. If clean air is part of the right to life, citizens also have a charter of duties to follow. The causes of pollution are well known. These straddle sectors, including industry, roads and buildings, vehicles, agriculture, shrinking green cover, municipal waste and urban living. However, citizens and their behaviour, in their varied roles as farmers, car and house owners, builders, contractors, and urban residents, remain at the centre. People complain and curse, and even silently suffer sickness from foul air, but sensitive and responsive behaviour remains elusive. The expansion of metro services and the availability of more public transport have not persuaded private car owners to switch. The Supreme Court went the extra mile by allowing firecrackers this Deepavali, while imposing justifiable restrictions on their toxic content and duration of use. Yet, citizens’ responses have not remotely matched the severity of the problem. It might seem contradictory, but many would like to reap all the dividends of GRAP without complying with its requirements.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #26 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 India’s recurring pollution crisis calls for a sustained movement for cleaner air

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 03:01:00 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: India’s fight against air pollution requires public engagement, effective communication and changes in civic behaviour; lessons from Swachh Bharat Mission offer a template for mobilising citizens to take ownership of clean air through collective action and responsible habits

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: D eepavali, the festival of lights, left a trail of dark smoke across large parts of India’s northern plains, especially around the national capital, Delhi, where 80 million people, particularly infants and the elderly, are struggling to breathe. The Air Quality Index (AQI) at several locations in the National Capital Region (NCR) had touched 400, indicating the severity of the conditions. Other cities and towns in the north, south, east and west, though better off than the NCR because of favourable weather and geographical advantages, do not have pristine air either. Air in most Indian cities contains pollutants, including particulate matter, at levels about eight times higher than the threshold set by the World Health Organization. The worst part of the problem is its dire predictability, except for concessions from the weather. The costly lessons from the capital have implications for the entire country. The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) swiftly moved up the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) from Stage I to Stage III within 15 days. The Commission, a statutory body established as an emergency response to toxic air conditions, has been cracking down on farm fires in Punjab, with its teams visiting fields to check incidents of stubble burning. PAVAN-I3C, the CAQM’s new Integrated Command and Control Centre, seeks to capture non-compliance in industries, traffic and transport systems and trigger immediate action against pollution spikes. Construction and demolition (C&D) activities have been halted until the 20th of this month. Inspections of construction sites and checks of Pollution Under Control Certificates (PUCC) are also vigorous. Last week, in an unprecedented move, CAQM directed Delhi and other NCR States to plan reduction of annual pollution levels by 15-20% forthwith. Regulatory moves, however essential, are not enough. Fines and work stoppages offer only partial deterrence, while obstructions and congestion on roads are an outright failure of enforcement. Institutional compliance, enforcement and monitoring by agencies are paramount, but civic behaviour is equally critical. The asks of people are not any great sacrifices, but some lifestyle retuning: use public transport and minimise use of personal vehicles, work from home, avoid construction activities for a few weeks, clean air filters at homes and in vehicles, avoid activities which generate dust, heat and smoke, and avoid open burning of solid waste and biomass. It would be unimaginable in many other countries for vehicle owners to be reminded of the pollution caused by their vehicles only during the months when the air becomes unbreathable. If clean air is part of the right to life, citizens also have a charter of duties to follow. The causes of pollution are well known. These straddle sectors, including industry, roads and buildings, vehicles, agriculture, shrinking green cover, municipal waste and urban living. However, citizens and their behaviour, in their varied roles as farmers, car and house owners, builders, contractors, and urban residents, remain at the centre. People complain and curse, and even silently suffer sickness from foul air, but sensitive and responsive behaviour remains elusive. The expansion of metro services and the availability of more public transport have not persuaded private car owners to switch. The Supreme Court went the extra mile by allowing firecrackers this Deepavali, while imposing justifiable restrictions on their toxic content and duration of use. Yet, citizens’ responses have not remotely matched the severity of the problem. It might seem contradictory, but many would like to reap all the dividends of GRAP without complying with its requirements.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: air pollution / New Delhi / The Hindu Explains / Text and Context / pollution / environmental pollution

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Enforcement (Noun)
सख्ती से कानून लागू करना — किसी नियम या आदेश का ज़मीनी स्तर पर पालन करवाना।
✓ Syn: Implementation, Execution, Administration  |  ✖ Ant: Neglect, Abandonment, Waiver
Predictably (Adverb)
जैसा पहले से अनुमान था — बिना किसी आश्चर्य के बिल्कुल पूर्वानुमान के मुताबिक होना।
✓ Syn: Foreseeably, Expectedly, Inevitably  |  ✖ Ant: Unexpectedly, Surprisingly, Abruptly
Environmental (Adjective)
पर्यावरण, प्रकृति और हमारे पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र (Ecosystem) से संबंधित।
✓ Syn: Ecological, Biospheric, Natural  |  ✖ Ant: Industrial, Polluting, Synthetic
Institutional (Adjective)
संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ।
✓ Syn: Systemic, Organizational, Constitutional  |  ✖ Ant: Individual, Informal, Unorganized

articles.title: Delhi court issues non-bailable warrant against Dhruv Rathee in 2018 defamation case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Judicial Magistrate Anam Rais Khan issued the warrant in a case filed by Vikas Sanskrityayan alias Vikas Pandey over a video uploaded on Dhruv Rathee's YouTube channel

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A Delhi court on Monday (November 23, 2026) issued a non-bailable warrant (NBW) against YouTuber Dhruv Rathee in a 2018 defamation case. Judicial Magistrate Anam Rais Khan issued the warrant in a case filed by Vikas Sanskrityayan alias Vikas Pandey over a video uploaded on Mr. Rathee's YouTube channel. The matter has been posted for further proceedings on December 3. A detailed order is awaited. Earlier on October 31, the court had issued fresh bailable warrants against Mr. Rathee. On October 17, it had issued bailable warrants against him after a process server reported that his house was locked while attempting to serve notice. The court had also issued fresh summons to Mr. Rathee at his address in Gurugram, Haryana. His advocate had submitted that Mr. Rathee ordinarily resides in Austria and had come to India for the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) protests in Delhi. The court had noted that Mr. Rathee was initially summoned in July 2019. The case pertains to a defamation complaint filed by Mr. Pandey in 2018 after Mr. Rathee uploaded a video against him on his YouTube channel.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: India / Delhi / judiciary (system of justice) / court

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #7 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Delhi court issues non-bailable warrant against Dhruv Rathee in 2018 defamation case

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 03:24:57 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Judicial Magistrate Anam Rais Khan issued the warrant in a case filed by Vikas Sanskrityayan alias Vikas Pandey over a video uploaded on Dhruv Rathee's YouTube channel

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A Delhi court on Monday (November 23, 2026) issued a non-bailable warrant (NBW) against YouTuber Dhruv Rathee in a 2018 defamation case. Judicial Magistrate Anam Rais Khan issued the warrant in a case filed by Vikas Sanskrityayan alias Vikas Pandey over a video uploaded on Mr. Rathee's YouTube channel. The matter has been posted for further proceedings on December 3. A detailed order is awaited. Earlier on October 31, the court had issued fresh bailable warrants against Mr. Rathee. On October 17, it had issued bailable warrants against him after a process server reported that his house was locked while attempting to serve notice. The court had also issued fresh summons to Mr. Rathee at his address in Gurugram, Haryana. His advocate had submitted that Mr. Rathee ordinarily resides in Austria and had come to India for the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) protests in Delhi. The court had noted that Mr. Rathee was initially summoned in July 2019. The case pertains to a defamation complaint filed by Mr. Pandey in 2018 after Mr. Rathee uploaded a video against him on his YouTube channel.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: India / Delhi / judiciary (system of justice) / court

✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. articles.title: India announces development package of 24,000 crore Nepalese Rupees for Nepal’s development
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: "The relations between India and Nepal stand as firm as the Himalayas and as vast as the oceans," says Nepal’s PM

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday (November 23, 2026) announced a development package of 24,000 crore Nepalese rupees for Nepal after holding wide-ranging talks with his Nepalese counterpart, Balendra Shah, that produced many key outcomes to further solidify the bilateral ties. The two leaders virtually laid the foundation of several India-assisted projects in Nepal and flagged off a cross-border passenger rail link between Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh and Janakpur Dham in Nepal. Nepal’s PM Shah landed in New Delhi on a two-day visit on Sunday (November 22), intending to inject new momentum into the bilateral ties that came under some strain in May following PM Shah's remarks seeking involvement of China and the United Kingdom to address the long-standing border dispute between India and Nepal. "The relations between India and Nepal stand as firm as the Himalayas and as vast as the oceans," the Nepalese leader said in his media statement. "As a dependable and trusted neighbour, India consistently stood as the first responder in times of natural disasters and difficult times in Nepal," he said, adding that mutual respect, steadfast trust and unbroken goodwill are the bedrock of the relations. In his remarks, Modi also highlighted the strength of India-Nepal ties and how New Delhi is committed to extend all possible support for development and prosperity of the neighbouring nation. "The relationship between India and Nepal is not merely that of neighbours, but it is about kinship and unbreakable trust. We share our joys and challenges," he said. "We are partners in each other's progress and a source of support for one another in difficult times," he said. The prime minister expressed India's deep condolences over the loss of lives caused by the devastating floods in Nepal in August. "And today, to give renewed strength to Nepal's reconstruction and long-term development, we announced a development cooperation package of 24,000 crore Nepalese rupees," he said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: PM Modi also made a mention of India's assistance to Nepal in the energy sector. "India has been a reliable supplier of petroleum products and other essential goods to Nepal for many years. In keeping with the spirit of our Neighbourhood First policy, despite serious challenges related to oil supply this year, we have maintained the supply of fuel, fertilisers and other essential goods to Nepal," he said.

hinglishTracks.en: "The relations between India and Nepal stand as firm as the Himalayas and as vast as the oceans," says Nepal’s PM
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — नेपाल के पीएम ने कहा, "भारत और नेपाल के बीच संबंध हिमालय जितने मजबूत और महासागर जितने विशाल हैं।"।

hinglishTracks.en: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday (November 23, 2026) announced a development package of 24,000 crore Nepalese rupees for Nepal after holding wide-ranging talks with his Nepalese counterpart, Balendra Shah, that produced many key outcomes to further solidify the bilateral ties.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — प्रधान मंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी ने सोमवार (23 नवंबर, 2026) को अपने नेपाली समकक्ष बालेंद्र शाह के साथ व्यापक बातचीत के बाद नेपाल के लिए 24,000 करोड़ नेपाली रुपये के विकास पैकेज की घोषणा की, जिससे द्विपक्षीय संबंधों को और मजबूत करने के लिए कई महत्वपूर्ण परिणाम सामने आए।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Bilateral' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: द्विपक्षीय — दो देशों के बीच आपसी समझौता, व्यापार या कूटनीतिक बातचीत। इसके Synonyms हैं: Reciprocal, Two-sided, Mutual और Antonyms हैं: Unilateral, Multilateral, One-way।

hinglishTracks.en: The two leaders virtually laid the foundation of several India-assisted projects in Nepal and flagged off a cross-border passenger rail link between Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh and Janakpur Dham in Nepal.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — दोनों नेताओं ने वस्तुतः नेपाल में कई भारत समर्थित परियोजनाओं की नींव रखी और उत्तर प्रदेश में अयोध्या और नेपाल में जनकपुर धाम के बीच सीमा पार यात्री रेल लिंक को हरी झंडी दिखाई।।

hinglishTracks.en: Nepal’s PM Shah landed in New Delhi on a two-day visit on Sunday (November 22), intending to inject new momentum into the bilateral ties that came under some strain in May following PM Shah's remarks seeking involvement of China and the United Kingdom to address the long-standing border dispute between India and Nepal.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — नेपाल के पीएम शाह रविवार (22 नवंबर) को दो दिवसीय यात्रा पर नई दिल्ली पहुंचे, जिसका इरादा द्विपक्षीय संबंधों में नई गति लाने का था, जो भारत और नेपाल के बीच लंबे समय से चले आ रहे सीमा विवाद को सुलझाने के लिए चीन और यूनाइटेड किंगडम को शामिल करने की पीएम शाह की टिप्पणी के बाद मई में कुछ तनाव में आ गए थे।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Bilateral' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: द्विपक्षीय — दो देशों के बीच आपसी समझौता, व्यापार या कूटनीतिक बातचीत। इसके Synonyms हैं: Reciprocal, Two-sided, Mutual और Antonyms हैं: Unilateral, Multilateral, One-way।

hinglishTracks.en: "The relations between India and Nepal stand as firm as the Himalayas and as vast as the oceans," the Nepalese leader said in his media statement.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — नेपाली नेता ने अपने मीडिया बयान में कहा, "भारत और नेपाल के बीच संबंध हिमालय जितने मजबूत और महासागर जितने विशाल हैं।"।

hinglishTracks.en: "As a dependable and trusted neighbour, India consistently stood as the first responder in times of natural disasters and difficult times in Nepal," he said, adding that mutual respect, steadfast trust and unbroken goodwill are the bedrock of the relations.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — उन्होंने कहा, ''एक भरोसेमंद और विश्वसनीय पड़ोसी के रूप में, भारत नेपाल में प्राकृतिक आपदाओं और कठिन समय में लगातार प्रथम प्रतिक्रियाकर्ता के रूप में खड़ा रहा।'' उन्होंने कहा कि आपसी सम्मान, दृढ़ विश्वास और अटूट सद्भावना संबंधों का आधार हैं।।

hinglishTracks.en: In his remarks, Modi also highlighted the strength of India-Nepal ties and how New Delhi is committed to extend all possible support for development and prosperity of the neighbouring nation.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — अपनी टिप्पणी में, मोदी ने भारत-नेपाल संबंधों की ताकत पर भी प्रकाश डाला और बताया कि कैसे नई दिल्ली पड़ोसी देश के विकास और समृद्धि के लिए हर संभव सहायता देने के लिए प्रतिबद्ध है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Development' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Development' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: "The relationship between India and Nepal is not merely that of neighbours, but it is about kinship and unbreakable trust.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — “भारत और नेपाल के बीच का रिश्ता सिर्फ पड़ोसियों का नहीं है, बल्कि यह रिश्तेदारी और अटूट विश्वास का है।।

hinglishTracks.en: We share our joys and challenges," he said.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — हम अपनी खुशियाँ और चुनौतियाँ साझा करते हैं," उन्होंने कहा।।

hinglishTracks.en: "We are partners in each other's progress and a source of support for one another in difficult times," he said.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — उन्होंने कहा, "हम एक-दूसरे की प्रगति में भागीदार हैं और कठिन समय में एक-दूसरे के समर्थन का स्रोत हैं।"।

hinglishTracks.en: The prime minister expressed India's deep condolences over the loss of lives caused by the devastating floods in Nepal in August.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — प्रधानमंत्री ने अगस्त में नेपाल में आई विनाशकारी बाढ़ से हुई जानमाल की हानि पर भारत की ओर से गहरी संवेदना व्यक्त की।।

hinglishTracks.en: "And today, to give renewed strength to Nepal's reconstruction and long-term development, we announced a development cooperation package of 24,000 crore Nepalese rupees," he said.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — उन्होंने कहा, "और आज, नेपाल के पुनर्निर्माण और दीर्घकालिक विकास को नई ताकत देने के लिए, हमने 24,000 करोड़ नेपाली रुपये के विकास सहयोग पैकेज की घोषणा की।"। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Reconstruction' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Reconstruction' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Significant, Substantial, Strategic और Antonyms हैं: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial।

hinglishTracks.en: PM Modi also made a mention of India's assistance to Nepal in the energy sector.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — पीएम मोदी ने ऊर्जा क्षेत्र में नेपाल को भारत की मदद का भी जिक्र किया.।

hinglishTracks.en: "India has been a reliable supplier of petroleum products and other essential goods to Nepal for many years.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — "भारत कई वर्षों से नेपाल को पेट्रोलियम उत्पादों और अन्य आवश्यक वस्तुओं का एक विश्वसनीय आपूर्तिकर्ता रहा है।।

hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — हमारी पड़ोसी प्रथम नीति की भावना को ध्यान में रखते हुए, इस वर्ष तेल आपूर्ति से संबंधित गंभीर चुनौतियों के बावजूद, हमने नेपाल को ईंधन, उर्वरक और अन्य आवश्यक वस्तुओं की आपूर्ति बनाए रखी है, ”उन्होंने कहा।।
