Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Shivamogga airport included in UDAN 6.0 tender process, says MP", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Raghavendra, Shivamogga MP, said that the Union government has decided to include Shivamogga airport in the revised UDAN 6.0 tender process.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Shivamogga airport included in UDAN 6.0 tender p' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Shivamogga airport included in UDAN 6.0 tende' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Shivamogga airport included in UDAN 6.0 tende' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Raghavendra, Shivamogga MP, said that the Union government has decided to include Shivamogga airport in the revised UDAN 6.0 tender process." (Hinglish Arth: शिवमोग्गा के सांसद राघवेंद्र ने कहा कि केंद्र सरकार ने शिवमोग्गा हवाई अड्डे को संशोधित UDAN 6.0 निविदा प्रक्रिया में शामिल करने का निर्णय लिया है।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Shivamogga airport included in UDAN 6.0 tender process, says MP"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. It was inaugurated in February 2023 and has been operating since August 2023.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "It was inaugurated in February 2023 and has been operating since August 2023." (Hinglish Arth: इसका उद्घाटन फरवरी 2023 में हुआ था और यह अगस्त 2023 से संचालित हो रहा है।)

articles.title: 3-member panel meet of KRMB ends without taking any decision on water use
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Telangana strongly opposed to AP’s demand for release of Nagarjunsagar water for use in Krishna Delta System

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The three-member committee of the Krishna River Management Board (KRMB) which met here on Monday to discuss the drinking water needs of the two member States — Andhra Pradesh and Telangana — for the next three months ended without taking any decision as Telangana strongly opposed A.P.’s indent of 19 tmc ft water, including 10 tmc ft for Krishna Delta System from Nagarjunasagar dam. The meeting chaired by Member-Secretary of the river board Satish Kumar Kamboj was attended by Engineers-in-Chief of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh O.V. Ramesh Babu and K. Narasimha Murthy. The meeting prolonged from forenoon to evening but no decision was taken as there was no consensus on utilisation of water available in Nagarjunsagar reservoir. In addition to the water indent placed by A.P. before the meeting for release of 9 tmc ft water from NS Right Canal, they also sought another 10 tmc ft water release from the reservoir for meeting the needs in the Krishna Delta System (KDS). On the other hand, Telangana asked for 21 tmc ft till February-end for drinking water needs of Hyderabad and other areas served by Nagarjunsagar. Telangana ENC strongly opposed the indent for 10 tmc ft water requirement for KDS stating that they would not allow even a drop of water to the system as water requirements of KDS were not linked to Nagarjunsagar reservoir releases. Speaking after the meeting, Mr. Ramesh Babu said even the 9 tmc ft water sought from the Right Canal was also not justifiable as A.P. has enough water stored in Pulichintala reservoir. He explained that Nagarjunsagar reservoir has only 45.4 tmc ft water above the minimum draw down level (MDDL) and of it 15 tmc ft is required for drinking needs of Hyderabad alone and the remaining 25 tmc ft was not sufficient to meet water unused so far by Telangana this water year. Further, he stated that Pulichintala has 26.75 tmc ft and Prakasam Barrage has another 2.44 tmc ft water available and water from Polavaram is also being drawn for the needs in the Krishna Basin through Pattiseema. There was no justification in A.P.’s demand for 19 tmc ft water as it had received good spells of rain due to the three recent cyclones, the Telangana ENC said. He stated that they asked for a full board meeting at the earliest to discuss all issues.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: As A.P. too stood ground with its demand suggesting that water could be drawn up to 490 ft level of Nagarjunsagar (534.4 ft level as at 6 pm on Monday), the three-member committee could not take any decision as Telangana insisted that water available in Nagarjunsagar below its MDDL was only for emergency needs.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #12 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 3-member panel meet of KRMB ends without taking any decision on water use

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 07:16:09 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Telangana strongly opposed to AP’s demand for release of Nagarjunsagar water for use in Krishna Delta System

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The three-member committee of the Krishna River Management Board (KRMB) which met here on Monday to discuss the drinking water needs of the two member States — Andhra Pradesh and Telangana — for the next three months ended without taking any decision as Telangana strongly opposed A.P.’s indent of 19 tmc ft water, including 10 tmc ft for Krishna Delta System from Nagarjunasagar dam. The meeting chaired by Member-Secretary of the river board Satish Kumar Kamboj was attended by Engineers-in-Chief of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh O.V. Ramesh Babu and K. Narasimha Murthy. The meeting prolonged from forenoon to evening but no decision was taken as there was no consensus on utilisation of water available in Nagarjunsagar reservoir. In addition to the water indent placed by A.P. before the meeting for release of 9 tmc ft water from NS Right Canal, they also sought another 10 tmc ft water release from the reservoir for meeting the needs in the Krishna Delta System (KDS). On the other hand, Telangana asked for 21 tmc ft till February-end for drinking water needs of Hyderabad and other areas served by Nagarjunsagar. Telangana ENC strongly opposed the indent for 10 tmc ft water requirement for KDS stating that they would not allow even a drop of water to the system as water requirements of KDS were not linked to Nagarjunsagar reservoir releases. Speaking after the meeting, Mr. Ramesh Babu said even the 9 tmc ft water sought from the Right Canal was also not justifiable as A.P. has enough water stored in Pulichintala reservoir. He explained that Nagarjunsagar reservoir has only 45.4 tmc ft water above the minimum draw down level (MDDL) and of it 15 tmc ft is required for drinking needs of Hyderabad alone and the remaining 25 tmc ft was not sufficient to meet water unused so far by Telangana this water year. Further, he stated that Pulichintala has 26.75 tmc ft and Prakasam Barrage has another 2.44 tmc ft water available and water from Polavaram is also being drawn for the needs in the Krishna Basin through Pattiseema. There was no justification in A.P.’s demand for 19 tmc ft water as it had received good spells of rain due to the three recent cyclones, the Telangana ENC said. He stated that they asked for a full board meeting at the earliest to discuss all issues.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: As A.P. too stood ground with its demand suggesting that water could be drawn up to 490 ft level of Nagarjunsagar (534.4 ft level as at 6 pm on Monday), the three-member committee could not take any decision as Telangana insisted that water available in Nagarjunsagar below its MDDL was only for emergency needs.

Justification (Noun)
औचित्य — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Justification' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Utilisation (Noun)
उपयोग — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Utilisation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Requirement (Adjective)
मांग — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Requirement' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Management (Adjective)
प्रबंध — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Management' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "3-member panel meet of KRMB ends without taking any decision on water use", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Telangana strongly opposed to AP’s demand for release of Nagarjunsagar water for use in Krishna Delta System.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of '3-member panel meet of KRMB ends without taking ' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to '3-member panel meet of KRMB ends without taki' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that '3-member panel meet of KRMB ends without taki' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Telangana strongly opposed to AP’s demand for release of Nagarjunsagar water for use in Krishna Delta System." D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "too stood ground with its demand suggesting that water could be drawn up to 490 ft level of Nagarjunsagar (534.4 ft level as at 6 pm on Monday), the..." (Hinglish Arth: भी अपनी मांग पर कायम रही कि नागार्जुनसागर के 490 फीट स्तर (सोमवार शाम 6 बजे तक 534.4 फीट स्तर) तक पानी खींचा जा सकता है, तीन सदस्यीय समिति तेलंगाना के आग्रह के कारण कोई निर्णय नहीं ले सकी।)

articles.title: SBI, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank retain D-SIB status; RBI maintains capital requirements
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The additional capital requirements are intended to enhance the resilience of these institutions.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has retained State Bank of India (SBI), HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank in its 2026 list of Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs), maintaining their respective positions under the same bucketing structure as in 2025. Under the RBI’s framework, SBI, placed in Bucket 4, will have to maintain an additional Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital requirement of 0.80% of its Risk Weighted Assets (RWAs). HDFC Bank, classified under Bucket 2, will have an additional CET1 requirement of 0.40%, while ICICI Bank, placed in Bucket 1, will have to maintain 0.20%. These additional capital requirements are over and above the Capital Conservation Buffer, strengthening the banks’ ability to absorb financial shocks and contain systemic risks. The latest classification is based on data collected from banks as of March 31, 2026. Under the D-SIB framework, banks are categorised into different buckets according to their Systemic Importance Scores (SISs), with higher scores attracting higher additional capital requirements. The RBI introduced the Framework for Dealing with D-SIBs on July 22, 2014, subsequently updating it on December 28, 2023. The framework requires the central bank to publicly disclose the names of designated D-SIBs annually, beginning in 2015, and assign them to appropriate buckets based on their systemic importance. SBI and ICICI Bank were initially designated as D-SIBs in 2015 and 2016, respectively. HDFC Bank joined the list in 2017, when all three banks were identified as systemically important financial institutions.

These additional capital requirements are over and above the Capital Conservation Buffer, strengthening the banks’ ability to absorb financial shocks and contain systemic risks. The latest classification is based on data collected from banks as of March 31, 2026. Under the D-SIB framework, banks are categorised into different buckets according to their Systemic Importance Scores (SISs), with higher scores attracting higher additional capital requirements. The RBI introduced the Framework for Dealing with D-SIBs on July 22, 2014, subsequently updating it on December 28, 2023. The framework requires the central bank to publicly disclose the names of designated D-SIBs annually, beginning in 2015, and assign them to appropriate buckets based on their systemic importance. SBI and ICICI Bank were initially designated as D-SIBs in 2015 and 2016, respectively. HDFC Bank joined the list in 2017, when all three banks were identified as systemically important financial institutions.

articles.title: Zelenskyy calls for four-way talks with Russia ‘as soon as possible’
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: During a gathering of Ukrainian supporters in Berlin last week, U.S. envoy Jared Kushner said that Washington might consider offering Ukraine a security guarantee similar to that provided under Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty as part of a peace settlement.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Monday (November 23, 2026) called for new negotiations with Russia involving European leaders to be held as soon as possible and repeated a plea for his country to join the NATO alliance. Mr. Zelenskyy, speaking by video to a gathering of lawmakers from NATO countries in Berlin, welcomed the latest push for peace talks with Moscow. "We must do everything to make sure that the four-party meeting - Ukraine, Europe, America and Russia - happens as soon as possible. We are ready to do this. Literally tomorrow," Mr. Zelenskyy said. "We have heard from our partners that they want to try to make it happen before Christmas. We hope it happens sooner." European governments have been excluded from past discussions and their push to join talks has gained prominence in recent weeks. Mr. Zelenskyy, whose country has been battling a full-scale Russian invasion since February 2022, has repeatedly called for a path to full membership in NATO - and not simply receiving security guarantees from alliance countries. He argued that Ukraine's combat experience, innovative defence industry and large military would all benefit other allies. "NATO is the answer - and with a strong Ukrainian army, NATO itself is guaranteed to be stronger," Mr. Zelenskyy told the Berlin gathering. A number of NATO leaders have expressed hesitation about bringing Ukraine into the alliance.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte, speaking after Mr. Zelenskyy at the same event on Monday, underscored the alliance's support for Ukraine but noted that joining would require unanimous support.

📰 Zelenskyy calls for four-way talks with Russia ‘as soon as possible’

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 08:48:20 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: During a gathering of Ukrainian supporters in Berlin last week, U.S. envoy Jared Kushner said that Washington might consider offering Ukraine a security guarantee similar to that provided under Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty as part of a peace settlement.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Monday (November 23, 2026) called for new negotiations with Russia involving European leaders to be held as soon as possible and repeated a plea for his country to join the NATO alliance. Mr. Zelenskyy, speaking by video to a gathering of lawmakers from NATO countries in Berlin, welcomed the latest push for peace talks with Moscow. "We must do everything to make sure that the four-party meeting - Ukraine, Europe, America and Russia - happens as soon as possible. We are ready to do this. Literally tomorrow," Mr. Zelenskyy said. "We have heard from our partners that they want to try to make it happen before Christmas. We hope it happens sooner." European governments have been excluded from past discussions and their push to join talks has gained prominence in recent weeks. Mr. Zelenskyy, whose country has been battling a full-scale Russian invasion since February 2022, has repeatedly called for a path to full membership in NATO - and not simply receiving security guarantees from alliance countries. He argued that Ukraine's combat experience, innovative defence industry and large military would all benefit other allies. "NATO is the answer - and with a strong Ukrainian army, NATO itself is guaranteed to be stronger," Mr. Zelenskyy told the Berlin gathering. A number of NATO leaders have expressed hesitation about bringing Ukraine into the alliance.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte, speaking after Mr. Zelenskyy at the same event on Monday, underscored the alliance's support for Ukraine but noted that joining would require unanimous support.

• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Monday (November 23, 2026) called for new negotiations with Russia involving European leaders to be held as soon as possible and repeated a plea for his country to join the NATO alliance. Mr. Zelenskyy, speaking by video to a gathering of lawmakers from NATO countries in Berlin, welcomed the latest push for peace talks with Moscow. "We must do everything to make sure that the four-party meeting - Ukraine, Europe, America and Russia - happens as soon as possible. We are ready to do this. Literally tomorrow," Mr. Zelenskyy said. "We have heard from our partners that they want to try to make it happen before Christmas. We hope it happens sooner." European governments have been excluded from past discussions and their push to join talks has gained prominence in recent weeks. Mr. Zelenskyy, whose country has been battling a full-scale Russian invasion since February 2022, has repeatedly called for a path to full membership in NATO - and not simply receiving security guarantees from alliance countries. He argued that Ukraine's combat experience, innovative defence industry and large military would all benefit other allies. "NATO is the answer - and with a strong Ukrainian army, NATO itself is guaranteed to be stronger," Mr. Zelenskyy told the Berlin gathering. A number of NATO leaders have expressed hesitation about bringing Ukraine into the alliance.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte, speaking after Mr. Zelenskyy at the same event on Monday, underscored the alliance's support for Ukraine but noted that joining would require unanimous support.

articles.title: Study finds PTSD-specific brain changes, paving way for personalised treatment
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The study uncovered specific changes in the brain linked to PTSD

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A new study has found that DNA methylation, a natural process that acts like a "dimmer switch" to turn genes down or completely off, varies more than expected across different brain regions in genes linked to PTSD. Stress and trauma can leave molecular marks in the brain that may help explain the development of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), a mental health disorder in which one experiences flashbacks or nightmares of a terrifying or life-threatening event. The study, published in the journal ' Cell Reports' , also found that among people affected by PTSD, the molecular variations appeared to be driven by a number of factors, including the sex and race of the person, and whether the trauma exposure occurred in childhood or adulthood. "The question that our research aims to address is 'What is really different about the PTSD brain?'" corresponding author Frances Champagne of the University of Texas at Austin, US, said. "The study found greater variation in DNA methylation patterns across brain regions in people with PTSD than in people with major depressive disorder. It also revealed considerable differences among individuals with PTSD," Champagne said. The findings could open the door to more individualised treatment options for people with PTSD in the future, the researchers said. A detailed methylation profiling was done of postmortem brains from 302 people -- 101 with PTSD, 100 without psychiatric disorders and 101 with major depressive disorder. Three different regions of brain were analysed in each sample: the prefrontal cortex, involved in higher level functions, including decision-making, the amygdala or the emotional centre of the brain, and the hippocampus, which manages memory. The study uncovered specific changes in the brain linked to PTSD, including a relative reduction in oligodendrocytes -- cells that form the protective covering of neurons (myelin sheath) -- in the amygdala of people with PTSD, particularly in those exposed to trauma in adulthood.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: PTSD was also associated with more pronounced DNA methylation differences in the prefrontal cortex, while major depressive disorder was associated with methylation differences in the amygdala.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #28 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Study finds PTSD-specific brain changes, paving way for personalised treatment

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 07:36:22 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The study uncovered specific changes in the brain linked to PTSD

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A new study has found that DNA methylation, a natural process that acts like a "dimmer switch" to turn genes down or completely off, varies more than expected across different brain regions in genes linked to PTSD. Stress and trauma can leave molecular marks in the brain that may help explain the development of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), a mental health disorder in which one experiences flashbacks or nightmares of a terrifying or life-threatening event. The study, published in the journal ' Cell Reports' , also found that among people affected by PTSD, the molecular variations appeared to be driven by a number of factors, including the sex and race of the person, and whether the trauma exposure occurred in childhood or adulthood. "The question that our research aims to address is 'What is really different about the PTSD brain?'" corresponding author Frances Champagne of the University of Texas at Austin, US, said. "The study found greater variation in DNA methylation patterns across brain regions in people with PTSD than in people with major depressive disorder. It also revealed considerable differences among individuals with PTSD," Champagne said. The findings could open the door to more individualised treatment options for people with PTSD in the future, the researchers said. A detailed methylation profiling was done of postmortem brains from 302 people -- 101 with PTSD, 100 without psychiatric disorders and 101 with major depressive disorder. Three different regions of brain were analysed in each sample: the prefrontal cortex, involved in higher level functions, including decision-making, the amygdala or the emotional centre of the brain, and the hippocampus, which manages memory. The study uncovered specific changes in the brain linked to PTSD, including a relative reduction in oligodendrocytes -- cells that form the protective covering of neurons (myelin sheath) -- in the amygdala of people with PTSD, particularly in those exposed to trauma in adulthood.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: PTSD was also associated with more pronounced DNA methylation differences in the prefrontal cortex, while major depressive disorder was associated with methylation differences in the amygdala.

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The objective is not merely to ensure that children wear spectacles, but that the prescription is appropriate, the lenses are correctly dispensed and their vision is monitored as they grow

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: An incorrect or outdated spectacles prescription can leave a child’s vision inadequately corrected, affecting classroom activities and learning. Regular eye examinations are important because children’s eyesight can change as they grow, and wearing spectacles alone does not ensure that their vision is being corrected properly.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: A study of 5,268 school-going children in north India found that only 23.03% of those prescribed spectacles were using the correct prescription. Inaccurate spectacle power was common, with younger age and longer duration of spectacle use among the associated factors.

articles.title: Bausch + Lomb's eye-drop drug fails to reduce pain after laser surgery in trial
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Bausch + Lomb said it plans to discuss the results with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration as it considers next steps for the drug, including a potential late-stage trial

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Bausch + Lomb said on Thursday its experimental eye-drop treatment failed to show a significant reduction in pain over the first 24 hours after laser eye surgery in a mid-stage study. However, the drug showed signs of benefit in secondary and exploratory analyses, including greater pain relief shortly after surgery and faster corneal healing. The mid-stage trial tested two doses of BL1332 in 129 patients undergoing photorefractive keratectomy (PRK), a laser procedure used to correct vision. At six hours after surgery, complete pain relief was reported by 14% and 14.6% of patients receiving the two doses, compared with 3.7% of patients receiving a placebo. Ocular surface pain is a common complication of eye surgery and certain eye diseases. The company said there are currently no approved treatments that directly target its underlying nerve pathways.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Bausch + Lomb said it plans to discuss the results with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration as it considers next steps for the drug, including a potential late-stage trial. Shares of the eye-care company fell 1.4% in extended trading.

• 1. Core Context & Background: Bausch + Lomb said it plans to discuss the results with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration as it considers next steps for the drug, including a potential late-stage trial
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Bausch + Lomb said on Thursday its experimental eye-drop treatment failed to show a significant reduction in pain over the first 24 hours after laser eye surgery in a mid-stage study. However, the drug showed signs of benefit in secondary and exploratory analyses, including greater pain relief shortly after surgery and faster corneal healing. The mid-stage trial tested two doses of BL1332 in 129 patients undergoing photorefractive keratectomy (PRK), a laser procedure used to correct vision. At six hours after surgery, complete pain relief was reported by 14% and 14.6% of patients receiving the two doses, compared with 3.7% of patients receiving a placebo. Ocular surface pain is a common complication of eye surgery and certain eye diseases. The company said there are currently no approved treatments that directly target its underlying nerve pathways.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Bausch + Lomb said it plans to discuss the results with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration as it considers next steps for the drug, including a potential late-stage trial. Shares of the eye-care company fell 1.4% in extended trading.

articles.title: Antimicrobial overuse could make common infections harder to treat: Health ministry official
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: World AMR Awareness Week is observed from November 18 to 24 every year to improve awareness and understanding of antimicrobial resistance and promote best practices among the public, policymakers and One Health stakeholders

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Misuse and overuse of antimicrobials could undermine decades of medical progress and make even common infections increasingly difficult to treat, a senior health ministry official said on Wednesday, calling for collective action to contain antimicrobial resistance (AMR). Addressing the national observance of World Antimicrobial Resistance Awareness Week 2026 virtually, Union Health Secretary Punya Salila Srivastava described AMR as one of the most serious public health challenges and stressed the need for a coordinated "One Health" approach to tackle it. This year's theme is "One Health, One Action: Prevent AMR Now". She said medicines that have saved countless lives are gradually losing their effectiveness due to misuse and overuse. Srivastava highlighted the interconnectedness of human and animal health, plant and food systems and the environment, noting that improper use of antimicrobials across these sectors contributes to the emergence and spread of resistance. She said the government has accorded high priority to containing AMR, with the National Action Plan on Antimicrobial Resistance 2.0 (NAP AMR 2.0), 2025-2029, providing a framework for surveillance, infection prevention, responsible antimicrobial use, research and coordinated action. The health ministry's National Programme on AMR Containment, coordinated by the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), focuses on strengthening laboratory capacity for AMR surveillance, infection prevention and control, antimicrobial stewardship and awareness generation, she said. Srivastava urged healthcare professionals to prescribe antibiotics only when clinically indicated and in accordance with treatment guidelines. She also asked pharmacists to ensure appropriate dispensing against valid prescriptions and counsel patients on their correct use. She also advised people against self-medication, sharing antibiotics or using leftover medicines, stressing that antibiotics are not effective against viral infections such as the common cold and influenza.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: More than half of antimicrobial sales in India take place without prescriptions, while nearly half of outpatient antibiotic prescriptions are inappropriate, participants at the event noted.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #29 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Antimicrobial overuse could make common infections harder to treat: Health ministry official

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 06:19:39 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: World AMR Awareness Week is observed from November 18 to 24 every year to improve awareness and understanding of antimicrobial resistance and promote best practices among the public, policymakers and One Health stakeholders

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Misuse and overuse of antimicrobials could undermine decades of medical progress and make even common infections increasingly difficult to treat, a senior health ministry official said on Wednesday, calling for collective action to contain antimicrobial resistance (AMR). Addressing the national observance of World Antimicrobial Resistance Awareness Week 2026 virtually, Union Health Secretary Punya Salila Srivastava described AMR as one of the most serious public health challenges and stressed the need for a coordinated "One Health" approach to tackle it. This year's theme is "One Health, One Action: Prevent AMR Now". She said medicines that have saved countless lives are gradually losing their effectiveness due to misuse and overuse. Srivastava highlighted the interconnectedness of human and animal health, plant and food systems and the environment, noting that improper use of antimicrobials across these sectors contributes to the emergence and spread of resistance. She said the government has accorded high priority to containing AMR, with the National Action Plan on Antimicrobial Resistance 2.0 (NAP AMR 2.0), 2025-2029, providing a framework for surveillance, infection prevention, responsible antimicrobial use, research and coordinated action. The health ministry's National Programme on AMR Containment, coordinated by the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), focuses on strengthening laboratory capacity for AMR surveillance, infection prevention and control, antimicrobial stewardship and awareness generation, she said. Srivastava urged healthcare professionals to prescribe antibiotics only when clinically indicated and in accordance with treatment guidelines. She also asked pharmacists to ensure appropriate dispensing against valid prescriptions and counsel patients on their correct use. She also advised people against self-medication, sharing antibiotics or using leftover medicines, stressing that antibiotics are not effective against viral infections such as the common cold and influenza.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: More than half of antimicrobial sales in India take place without prescriptions, while nearly half of outpatient antibiotic prescriptions are inappropriate, participants at the event noted.

articles.title: England launches world's largest AI-aided breast cancer screening trial
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Women attending routine breast screening at 30 planned sites nationwide will be given details about the trial and participate, unless they choose to opt out

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: England's state-run health service said Monday it has launched the world's largest AI-assisted breast cancer screening trial, which is set to involve nearly 700,000 women over the next three years. The National Health Service (NHS) hailed the new trial as having the potential to transform breast cancer diagnosis, as it announced hundreds of women had been invited to take part at the outset. The £10 million ($13 million) programme will assess if tools assisted by artificial intelligence can help improve early cancer detection in screening, which health officials hope will then free up specialist clinicians' time. The AI-assisted reading tool will assist clinicians in reviewing images collected from routine mammograms, according to the NHS. "This is the biggest AI breast cancer trial in the world," Health Secretary Yvette Cooper said in a statement, lauding the tech's "huge potential" while pledging "proper safeguards" to ensure safety and effectiveness. "If successful, this technology could help women get a breast cancer diagnosis and start treatment much more quickly, giving them the best possible chance of recovery." The trial is being led by the University of Warwick, the University of Cambridge and Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, working closely with NHS England. Women attending routine breast screening at 30 planned sites nationwide will be given details about the trial and participate, unless they choose to opt out. The NHS stressed screening appointments will proceed as normal, but the AI-assisted tool will be used alongside specialists checking the images to look for cancers that are too small to see or feel.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The trial will test whether AI-assisted tools could allow most images to be reviewed by only one specialist, rather than the current two.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #30 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 England launches world's largest AI-aided breast cancer screening trial

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 06:15:31 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Women attending routine breast screening at 30 planned sites nationwide will be given details about the trial and participate, unless they choose to opt out

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: England's state-run health service said Monday it has launched the world's largest AI-assisted breast cancer screening trial, which is set to involve nearly 700,000 women over the next three years. The National Health Service (NHS) hailed the new trial as having the potential to transform breast cancer diagnosis, as it announced hundreds of women had been invited to take part at the outset. The £10 million ($13 million) programme will assess if tools assisted by artificial intelligence can help improve early cancer detection in screening, which health officials hope will then free up specialist clinicians' time. The AI-assisted reading tool will assist clinicians in reviewing images collected from routine mammograms, according to the NHS. "This is the biggest AI breast cancer trial in the world," Health Secretary Yvette Cooper said in a statement, lauding the tech's "huge potential" while pledging "proper safeguards" to ensure safety and effectiveness. "If successful, this technology could help women get a breast cancer diagnosis and start treatment much more quickly, giving them the best possible chance of recovery." The trial is being led by the University of Warwick, the University of Cambridge and Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, working closely with NHS England. Women attending routine breast screening at 30 planned sites nationwide will be given details about the trial and participate, unless they choose to opt out. The NHS stressed screening appointments will proceed as normal, but the AI-assisted tool will be used alongside specialists checking the images to look for cancers that are too small to see or feel.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The trial will test whether AI-assisted tools could allow most images to be reviewed by only one specialist, rather than the current two.

✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
University (Adjective / Verb)
विश्वविद्यालय — इस अनुच्छेद में 'University' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
Foundation (Noun)
नींव — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Foundation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🚀 Science, Tech & Environment passage on "England launches world's largest AI-aided breast cancer screening trial", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Women attending routine breast screening at 30 planned sites nationwide will be given details about the trial and participate, unless they choose to...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'England launches world's largest AI-aided breast' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'England launches world's largest AI-aided bre' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'England launches world's largest AI-aided bre' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Women attending routine breast screening at 30 planned sites nationwide will be given details about the trial and participate, unless they choose to..." Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "England launches world's largest AI-aided breast cancer screening trial"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. The trial will test whether AI-assisted tools could allow most images to be reviewed by only one specialist, rather than the current two.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "The trial will test whether AI-assisted tools could allow most images to be reviewed by only one specialist, rather than the current two." articles.title: DPS’s NCC cadets visit Bharat Cancer Hospital in Mysuru as part of community outreach programme
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The NCC cadets of Delhi Public School (DPS), Mysuru, undertook a community outreach visit to Bharat Cancer Hospital in the city as part of their endeavour to inculcate values of social responsibility, compassion and service among cadets.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: During the recent visit, the cadets distributed fruit to patients and spent time interacting with them. The experience offered the young cadets a deeper understanding of the challenges faced by cancer patients, while highlighting the importance of health, emotional support, kindness and human dignity, according to a press statement here. The visit served as a meaningful learning experience, sensitising cadets to the importance of empathy, compassion and solidarity with people facing difficult circumstances. It also reinforced their sense of responsibility towards society and encouraged them to extend care and support beyond the confines of their school and personal lives, the statement added.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The visit was conducted under the guidance of Second Officer Mamatha Prasad M., Associate NCC Officer, DPS, Mysuru.

articles.title: ACB conducts surprise checks at NIMS, flags irregularities across departments
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB), Telangana, along with officials from TG Safe (Food Safety), the Drug Control Department and the Labour Department, conducted surprise checks at Nizam’s Institute of Medical Sciences (NIMS), Panjagutta, on October 29 and November 2, and found several irregularities in the functioning of the hospital.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The tender process for manpower services was not completed during the period between 2019 and 2025. Violations were noticed in the appointment of workers and their conversion to the semi-skilled category, with indications of possible collusion in recruitment-related activities. The main canteen was found functioning in unhygienic conditions, with expired food items and without FSSAI registration. Labour law violations and irregularities in the canteen tender process were also noticed. Preliminary scrutiny indicated possible anti-competitive practices and collusion among bidders. Medical shops were not maintaining mandatory sale records and were employing unregistered workers. The tender process for allotment of the shops is also under scrutiny. The ACB noticed abnormal delays in finalising security service tenders and repeated extensions of contracts. A bank guarantee of ₹28.13 lakh belonging to a defaulting agency had not been forfeited. During verification of five operation theatres, vendors were found storing a large quantity of implants and consignment items, worth approximately ₹5 crore, in almirahs near the operation theatres and in OT sub-stores without authorisation and in violation of prescribed procedures. Doctors and nursing staff were found taking implants directly from vendors without raising an indent to the main store. After use, doctors would raise utility certificates and send them to the main store along with the vendors’ invoices for billing. The ACB said the procedure was contrary to prescribed norms and left scope for collusion with suppliers, including the possibility of raising utility certificates for implants that were never used but were billed. In several cases, bills were processed after patients had been discharged, particularly those covered under the Aarogyasri scheme, whose payments are made by the government. In some instances, bills were processed as late as three months after the patient’s death. Billing entries worth approximately ₹66 lakh were made after the discharge of patients during July, August and September.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The ACB also noticed abnormally high usage of surgical consumables. Records showed 800 gloves being used for one patient in a week. Most of the irregularities related to patients admitted under the Aarogyasri scheme. Note files, agreement copies and other related documents were seized during the checks for further verification and confirmation of the allegations.

hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — भ्रष्टाचार निरोधक ब्यूरो (एसीबी), तेलंगाना ने टीजी सेफ (खाद्य सुरक्षा), औषधि नियंत्रण विभाग और श्रम विभाग के अधिकारियों के साथ, 29 अक्टूबर और 2 नवंबर को निज़ाम इंस्टीट्यूट ऑफ मेडिकल साइंसेज (एनआईएमएस), पंजागुट्टा में औचक निरीक्षण किया और अस्पताल के कामकाज में कई अनियमितताएं पाईं।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Institutional' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ। इसके Synonyms हैं: Systemic, Organizational, Constitutional और Antonyms हैं: Individual, Informal, Unorganized।

hinglishTracks.en: The tender process for manpower services was not completed during the period between 2019 and 2025.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — 2019 और 2025 के बीच की अवधि के दौरान जनशक्ति सेवाओं के लिए निविदा प्रक्रिया पूरी नहीं की गई थी।।

hinglishTracks.en: Violations were noticed in the appointment of workers and their conversion to the semi-skilled category, with indications of possible collusion in recruitment-related activities.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — भर्ती संबंधी गतिविधियों में संभावित मिलीभगत के संकेत के साथ श्रमिकों की नियुक्ति और उन्हें अर्ध-कुशल श्रेणी में परिवर्तित करने में उल्लंघन देखा गया।।

hinglishTracks.en: Labour law violations and irregularities in the canteen tender process were also noticed.

hinglishTracks.en: The ACB said the procedure was contrary to prescribed norms and left scope for collusion with suppliers, including the possibility of raising utility certificates for implants that were never used but were billed.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — एसीबी ने कहा कि प्रक्रिया निर्धारित मानदंडों के विपरीत थी और आपूर्तिकर्ताओं के साथ मिलीभगत की गुंजाइश छोड़ती थी, जिसमें उन प्रत्यारोपणों के लिए उपयोगिता प्रमाण पत्र प्राप्त करने की संभावना भी शामिल थी जिनका कभी उपयोग नहीं किया गया था लेकिन उनका बिल बना दिया गया था।।

hinglishTracks.en: In several cases, bills were processed after patients had been discharged, particularly those covered under the Aarogyasri scheme, whose payments are made by the government.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — कई मामलों में, मरीजों को छुट्टी मिलने के बाद बिलों पर कार्रवाई की गई, विशेष रूप से आरोग्यश्री योजना के तहत आने वाले मरीजों का, जिनका भुगतान सरकार द्वारा किया जाता है।।

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #8 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 ACB conducts surprise checks at NIMS, flags irregularities across departments

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 09:27:28 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB), Telangana, along with officials from TG Safe (Food Safety), the Drug Control Department and the Labour Department, conducted surprise checks at Nizam’s Institute of Medical Sciences (NIMS), Panjagutta, on October 29 and November 2, and found several irregularities in the functioning of the hospital.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The tender process for manpower services was not completed during the period between 2019 and 2025. Violations were noticed in the appointment of workers and their conversion to the semi-skilled category, with indications of possible collusion in recruitment-related activities. The main canteen was found functioning in unhygienic conditions, with expired food items and without FSSAI registration. Labour law violations and irregularities in the canteen tender process were also noticed. Preliminary scrutiny indicated possible anti-competitive practices and collusion among bidders. Medical shops were not maintaining mandatory sale records and were employing unregistered workers. The tender process for allotment of the shops is also under scrutiny. The ACB noticed abnormal delays in finalising security service tenders and repeated extensions of contracts. A bank guarantee of ₹28.13 lakh belonging to a defaulting agency had not been forfeited. During verification of five operation theatres, vendors were found storing a large quantity of implants and consignment items, worth approximately ₹5 crore, in almirahs near the operation theatres and in OT sub-stores without authorisation and in violation of prescribed procedures. Doctors and nursing staff were found taking implants directly from vendors without raising an indent to the main store. After use, doctors would raise utility certificates and send them to the main store along with the vendors’ invoices for billing. The ACB said the procedure was contrary to prescribed norms and left scope for collusion with suppliers, including the possibility of raising utility certificates for implants that were never used but were billed. In several cases, bills were processed after patients had been discharged, particularly those covered under the Aarogyasri scheme, whose payments are made by the government. In some instances, bills were processed as late as three months after the patient’s death. Billing entries worth approximately ₹66 lakh were made after the discharge of patients during July, August and September.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The ACB also noticed abnormally high usage of surgical consumables. Records showed 800 gloves being used for one patient in a week. Most of the irregularities related to patients admitted under the Aarogyasri scheme. Note files, agreement copies and other related documents were seized during the checks for further verification and confirmation of the allegations.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Quantitative (Adjective)
आंकड़ों और संख्या पर आधारित — जिसे ठोस नंबरों और डेटा में मापा जा सके।
✓ Syn: Measurable, Numerical, Empirical  |  ✖ Ant: Qualitative, Subjective, Unmeasurable
Institutional (Adjective)
संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ।
✓ Syn: Systemic, Organizational, Constitutional  |  ✖ Ant: Individual, Informal, Unorganized
Authorisation (Noun)
प्राधिकार — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Authorisation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Registration (Noun)
पंजीकरण — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Registration' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "ACB conducts surprise checks at NIMS, flags irregularities across departments", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB), Telangana, along with officials from TG Safe (Food Safety), the Drug Control Department and the Labour Department,...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'ACB conducts surprise checks at NIMS, flags irre' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'ACB conducts surprise checks at NIMS, flags i' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'ACB conducts surprise checks at NIMS, flags i' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB), Telangana, along with officials from TG Safe (Food Safety), the Drug Control Department and the Labour Department,..." (Hinglish Arth: भ्रष्टाचार निरोधक ब्यूरो (एसीबी), तेलंगाना ने टीजी सेफ (खाद्य सुरक्षा), औषधि नियंत्रण विभाग और श्रम विभाग के अधिकारियों के साथ, निज़ाम इंस्टीट्यूट ऑफ मेडिकल साइंसेज (एनआईएम) में औचक निरीक्षण किया।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "ACB conducts surprise checks at NIMS, flags irregularities across departments"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Note files, agreement copies and other related documents were seized during the checks for further verification and confirmation of the allegations.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Note files, agreement copies and other related documents were seized during the checks for further verification and confirmation of the allegations." (Hinglish Arth: आरोपों की आगे की जांच और पुष्टि के लिए जांच के दौरान नोट फाइलें, समझौते की प्रतियां और अन्य संबंधित दस्तावेज जब्त कर लिए गए।)

The main canteen was found functioning in unhygienic conditions, with expired food items and without FSSAI registration. Labour law violations and irregularities in the canteen tender process were also noticed. Preliminary scrutiny indicated possible anti-competitive practices and collusion among bidders. Medical shops were not maintaining mandatory sale records and were employing unregistered workers. The tender process for allotment of the shops is also under scrutiny. The ACB noticed abnormal delays in finalising security service tenders and repeated extensions of contracts. A bank guarantee of ₹28.13 lakh belonging to a defaulting agency had not been forfeited. During verification of five operation theatres, vendors were found storing a large quantity of implants and consignment items, worth approximately ₹5 crore, in almirahs near the operation theatres and in OT sub-stores without authorisation and in violation of prescribed procedures. Doctors and nursing staff were found taking implants directly from vendors without raising an indent to the main store. After use, doctors would raise utility certificates and send them to the main store along with the vendors’ invoices for billing. The ACB said the procedure was contrary to prescribed norms and left scope for collusion with suppliers, including the possibility of raising utility certificates for implants that were never used but were billed. In several cases, bills were processed after patients had been discharged, particularly those covered under the Aarogyasri scheme, whose payments are made by the government. In some instances, bills were processed as late as three months after the patient’s death. Billing entries worth approximately ₹66 lakh were made after the discharge of patients during July, August and September.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The ACB also noticed abnormally high usage of surgical consumables. Records showed 800 gloves being used for one patient in a week. Most of the irregularities related to patients admitted under the Aarogyasri scheme. Note files, agreement copies and other related documents were seized during the checks for further verification and confirmation of the allegations.

hinglishTracks.en: Former Supreme Court judge Jasti Chelameswar on Monday stressed on the need for people to understand and protect their constitutional rights while delivering the Kinjarapu Yerran Naidu Memorial Endowment Lecture at Andhra University.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — सुप्रीम कोर्ट के पूर्व न्यायाधीश जस्ती चेलमेश्वर ने सोमवार को आंध्र विश्वविद्यालय में किंजरापु येरन नायडू मेमोरियल एंडोमेंट व्याख्यान देते हुए लोगों को अपने संवैधानिक अधिकारों को समझने और उनकी रक्षा करने की आवश्यकता पर जोर दिया।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Constitutional' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप। इसके Synonyms हैं: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful और Antonyms हैं: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary।

hinglishTracks.en: Speaking on ‘Electoral Rights under the Indian Constitution’, he said the survival and protection of the Constitution rested in the hands of the people.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — 'भारतीय संविधान के तहत चुनावी अधिकार' पर बोलते हुए उन्होंने कहा कि संविधान का अस्तित्व और सुरक्षा लोगों के हाथों में है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Constitutional' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप। इसके Synonyms हैं: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful और Antonyms हैं: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary।

hinglishTracks.en: Describing the Constitution as a legal document that provides a framework for governance, he said elections were essential for the functioning of democracy and underscored the importance of the right to vote.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — संविधान को एक कानूनी दस्तावेज बताते हुए जो शासन के लिए एक रूपरेखा प्रदान करता है, उन्होंने कहा कि लोकतंत्र के कामकाज के लिए चुनाव आवश्यक थे और मतदान के अधिकार के महत्व को रेखांकित किया।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Constitutional' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप। इसके Synonyms हैं: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful और Antonyms हैं: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary।

hinglishTracks.en: He also emphasised the distinction between the right to contest elections and the right to vote.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — उन्होंने चुनाव लड़ने के अधिकार और वोट देने के अधिकार के बीच अंतर पर भी जोर दिया।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Distinction' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: भेद — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Distinction' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse और Antonyms हैं: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable।

hinglishTracks.en: Referring to election rules and practices adopted by various States, Justice Chelameswar cited related court cases and judgments.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — विभिन्न राज्यों द्वारा अपनाए गए चुनाव नियमों और प्रथाओं का जिक्र करते हुए, न्यायमूर्ति चेलमेश्वर ने संबंधित अदालती मामलों और निर्णयों का हवाला दिया।।

hinglishTracks.en: He also discussed the emerging jurisprudence on free and fair elections.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — उन्होंने स्वतंत्र और निष्पक्ष चुनावों पर उभरते न्यायशास्त्र पर भी चर्चा की।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Jurisprudence' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: न्यायशास्र सा — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Jurisprudence' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Significant, Substantial, Strategic और Antonyms हैं: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial।

hinglishTracks.en: Vice-Chancellor G.P.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — कुलपति जी.पी.।

hinglishTracks.en: Raja Sekhar presided over the programme.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — कार्यक्रम की अध्यक्षता राजा शेखर ने की.।

hinglishTracks.en: Law College Principal K.

hinglishTracks.en: Sita Manikyam spoke about the endowment established in memory of former Union Minister and Andhra University alumnus Kinjarapu Yerran Naidu.

• 1. Core Context & Background: Former Supreme Court judge Jasti Chelameswar on Monday stressed on the need for people to understand and protect their constitutional rights while delivering the Kinjarapu Yerran Naidu Memorial Endowment Lecture at Andhra University.
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Speaking on ‘Electoral Rights under the Indian Constitution’, he said the survival and protection of the Constitution rested in the hands of the people. Describing the Constitution as a legal document that provides a framework for governance, he said elections were essential for the functioning of democracy and underscored the importance of the right to vote. He also emphasised the distinction between the right to contest elections and the right to vote. Referring to election rules and practices adopted by various States, Justice Chelameswar cited related court cases and judgments. He also discussed the emerging jurisprudence on free and fair elections.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Vice-Chancellor G.P. Raja Sekhar presided over the programme. Law College Principal K. Sita Manikyam spoke about the endowment established in memory of former Union Minister and Andhra University alumnus Kinjarapu Yerran Naidu.

articles.title: Skin specialists in Keralam issue alert against fairness creams that promise instant action
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: It is important to ensure that the beauty products being used do not have any harmful effects on the body, say functionaries of the Indian Association of Dermatologists, Venereologists, and Leprologists

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Dermatologists in Keralam have urged the people to be careful about the use of cosmetics for beauty treatment in the wake of reports about a 17-year-old girl from Malappuram district developing kidney diseases after using a ‘mercury-laced’ fairness cream. Expressing their concerns over the incident, the State branch of the Indian Association of Dermatologists, Venereologists, and Leprologists (IADVL) said on Monday that the society should be alert against fairness creams that promise instant action. Vinod Nair, president, and Ebi Chacko, Secretary, IADVL Kerala, pointed out that the manufacturers of these creams most often don’t exhibit their ingredients. They may contain chemicals including mercury, which have the potential to cause serious damage not only to the skin but even to internal organs. In such a scenario, it is important to ensure that the beauty products being used do not have any harmful effects on the body. A resolution to this effect was passed at ‘CUTICON 2026’, a national conference of dermatologists held at Kannur recently. The resolution said that the consumers should not be deceived into purchasing unapproved creams based on advertisements circulating on social media that do not reflect the reality. Only qualified dermatologists should be consulted for skin conditions and cosmetic treatments. It should also be ensured that the doctors have recognised dermatology degrees such as MD, DNB, DDVL, or DVD. The IADVL functionaries said that the treatment by unqualified people can cause burns, scarring, pigmentation, infections and steroid damage. Lasers, peels and injectables should only be done by qualified dermatologists, they said. The girl from Malappuram developed membranous nephropathy, a kidney disease, after using the cream called F Tune for nearly a year. She was lured into buying the product by promotional videos of social media influencers, especially those on Instagram. The cream promised to remove dark spots, pimples, and pigmentation. However, lab results reportedly found 1.25% mercury, or 12,500 parts per million (ppm), in the cream though the permitted limit is less than 1 ppm. She developed low blood pressure, difficulty in walking, and swelling in her legs along with spells of fainting. It was also noticed that she was losing protein through urine in excessive amounts. According to sources, she has since recovered from that stage after medical treatment. The family is now planning legal recourse.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Soon after these reports emerged in the public domain, Mappilapattu singer Saleem Kodathoor too claimed that he had also gone through a similar situation after using a fairness cream. Its after-effects reportedly forced him to suspend music programmes for months. The State Drugs Control department has now swung into action to curb the sale of fake cosmetic products.

hinglishTracks.en: However, lab results reportedly found 1.25% mercury, or 12,500 parts per million (ppm), in the cream though the permitted limit is less than 1 ppm.

hinglishTracks.en: According to sources, she has since recovered from that stage after medical treatment.

hinglishTracks.en: Its after-effects reportedly forced him to suspend music programmes for months.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #10 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Skin specialists in Keralam issue alert against fairness creams that promise instant action

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 09:27:06 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: It is important to ensure that the beauty products being used do not have any harmful effects on the body, say functionaries of the Indian Association of Dermatologists, Venereologists, and Leprologists

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Dermatologists in Keralam have urged the people to be careful about the use of cosmetics for beauty treatment in the wake of reports about a 17-year-old girl from Malappuram district developing kidney diseases after using a ‘mercury-laced’ fairness cream. Expressing their concerns over the incident, the State branch of the Indian Association of Dermatologists, Venereologists, and Leprologists (IADVL) said on Monday that the society should be alert against fairness creams that promise instant action. Vinod Nair, president, and Ebi Chacko, Secretary, IADVL Kerala, pointed out that the manufacturers of these creams most often don’t exhibit their ingredients. They may contain chemicals including mercury, which have the potential to cause serious damage not only to the skin but even to internal organs. In such a scenario, it is important to ensure that the beauty products being used do not have any harmful effects on the body. A resolution to this effect was passed at ‘CUTICON 2026’, a national conference of dermatologists held at Kannur recently. The resolution said that the consumers should not be deceived into purchasing unapproved creams based on advertisements circulating on social media that do not reflect the reality. Only qualified dermatologists should be consulted for skin conditions and cosmetic treatments. It should also be ensured that the doctors have recognised dermatology degrees such as MD, DNB, DDVL, or DVD. The IADVL functionaries said that the treatment by unqualified people can cause burns, scarring, pigmentation, infections and steroid damage. Lasers, peels and injectables should only be done by qualified dermatologists, they said. The girl from Malappuram developed membranous nephropathy, a kidney disease, after using the cream called F Tune for nearly a year. She was lured into buying the product by promotional videos of social media influencers, especially those on Instagram. The cream promised to remove dark spots, pimples, and pigmentation. However, lab results reportedly found 1.25% mercury, or 12,500 parts per million (ppm), in the cream though the permitted limit is less than 1 ppm. She developed low blood pressure, difficulty in walking, and swelling in her legs along with spells of fainting. It was also noticed that she was losing protein through urine in excessive amounts. According to sources, she has since recovered from that stage after medical treatment. The family is now planning legal recourse.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Soon after these reports emerged in the public domain, Mappilapattu singer Saleem Kodathoor too claimed that he had also gone through a similar situation after using a fairness cream. Its after-effects reportedly forced him to suspend music programmes for months. The State Drugs Control department has now swung into action to curb the sale of fake cosmetic products.

✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Promotional (Adjective)
प्रचार — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Promotional' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Resolution (Noun)
संकल्प — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Resolution' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Skin specialists in Keralam issue alert against fairness creams that promise instant action", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. It is important to ensure that the beauty products being used do not have any harmful effects on the body, say functionaries of the Indian...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Skin specialists in Keralam issue alert against ' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Skin specialists in Keralam issue alert again' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Skin specialists in Keralam issue alert again' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "It is important to ensure that the beauty products being used do not have any harmful effects on the body, say functionaries of the Indian..." (Hinglish Arth: इंडियन एसोसिएशन ऑफ डर्मेटोलॉजिस्ट, वेनेरोलॉजिस्ट और लेप्रोलॉजिस्ट के पदाधिकारियों का कहना है कि यह सुनिश्चित करना महत्वपूर्ण है कि इस्तेमाल किए जा रहे सौंदर्य उत्पादों का शरीर पर कोई हानिकारक प्रभाव न पड़े।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Skin specialists in Keralam issue alert against fairness creams that promise instant action"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. The State Drugs Control department has now swung into action to curb the sale of fake cosmetic products.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "The State Drugs Control department has now swung into action to curb the sale of fake cosmetic products." (Hinglish Arth: नकली कॉस्मेटिक उत्पादों की बिक्री पर अंकुश लगाने के लिए राज्य औषधि नियंत्रण विभाग अब हरकत में आ गया है।)

articles.title: Over 10,000 applications received for changes in electoral roll during special camps held in Cuddalore
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: A total of 10,041 applications were received across the nine Assembly constituencies in Cuddalore district during the special camps held on November 21 and 22 for electoral roll inclusion, deletion and correction.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: According to officials, the camps were held at 2,590 polling stations at 1,327 locations across the nine Assembly segments in the district. Of these, 5,916 were Form 6 for new voter registration, 771 were Form 7 for deletion of names, and 3,354 were Form 8 for correction of entries. A total of 1,241 applications were filed from Chidambaram Assembly constituency, highest among Assembly segments.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: A total of 6,456 applications requesting various changes in the electoral roll were received by officials during the special camps held in seven Assembly constituencies in Villupuram district. The next special camp is scheduled on Sunday (November 29) and the final electoral roll will be released on January 4, 2027.

📰 Over 10,000 applications received for changes in electoral roll during special camps held in Cuddalore

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 09:25:17 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: A total of 10,041 applications were received across the nine Assembly constituencies in Cuddalore district during the special camps held on November 21 and 22 for electoral roll inclusion, deletion and correction.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: A total of 6,456 applications requesting various changes in the electoral roll were received by officials during the special camps held in seven Assembly constituencies in Villupuram district. articles.title: Influencers, sellers of unsafe cosmetics to face legal action
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The move follows the case of a 17-year-old girl from Malappuram who developed kidney disease after using a fairness cream laced with mercury

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The crackdown on spurious cosmetics continued in Keralam on Monday, with demands growing for State-wide inspections and legal action against those involved in their sale and promotion. The move follows the case of a 17-year-old girl from Malappuram who developed kidney disease after using a fairness cream laced with mercury. The girl had used the cream for about a year to remove dark patches on her face before developing health problems. She was diagnosed with membranous nephropathy, a serious kidney disorder. Health Minister K. Muraleedharan has sought legal action against social media influencers promoting fake and substandard cosmetics. In a letter to Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala, he urged him to direct the State Police Chief to identify those involved and initiate action against them. Mr. Muraleedharan said cosmetics containing excess chemicals were being promoted online through paid endorsements by celebrities and influencers. He warned that promoters, sellers and distributors would face legal action. He also urged the public not to be misled by such advertisements. Meanwhile, the Chief Minister’s office has asked the Health department to consider setting up special squads in all districts to check the sale and distribution of cosmetics containing mercury and other harmful chemicals. The directive followed a complaint by medical officer K. Prathibha, which flagged the difficulty in monitoring online sales, particularly products shipped from other States. The Indian Medical Association (IMA) has urged the Drugs Control department to conduct State-wide inspections, test suspicious cosmetics, seize unlicensed products and prosecute those responsible. It also called for a joint surveillance system involving the Health department, police, cybercrime wing and consumer protection authorities. The State branch of the Indian Association of Dermatologists, Venereologists and Leprologists (IADVL) has warned against fairness creams promising instant results. IADVL president Vinod Nair and secretary Ebi Chacko said manufacturers often failed to disclose ingredients, which could include mercury and other chemicals harmful to the skin and internal organs. Meanwhile, hepatologist Cyriac Abby Philips, popularly known as The LiverDoc on social media, named 10 influencers who allegedly promoted Vevoria’s F-Tune fairness cream. They were Jasmin Jaffar, Appu Vava, Amaya Vishnu, Sneha, Sukanya Harish, Reneesha Rahiman, Arunya Binu, Dilana Shinod, Asna Asharaf and Haritha Nambiar. Dr. Philips also urged Amazon to delist the cream, which was still available on the platform at ₹689 for a 30-gm pack. He noted that Vevoria had removed the cream’s Instagram profile. Actress and social media influencer Reneesha Rahiman has defended her decision to promote the fairness cream. Ms. Rahiman said she had tested the product on her own skin before endorsing it on social media. She said she was shocked to learn that the girl had developed serious health problems after using the cream.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Ms. Rahiman said she was not someone who promoted products simply for money and had agreed to the endorsement only after using the cream and being satisfied with the results. The promotion was carried out about a year ago, she said.
