articles.title: Armenia drops Nagorno-Karabakh claim in proposed new constitution
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The draft deletes the 1990 preamble, which included a clause for re-unification with the Nagorno-Karabakh region and called for the international recognition of the genocide of Armenians by the Ottoman Empire

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Armenian leader Nikol Pashinyan unveiled a draft constitution on Monday (November 23, 2026) that would get rid of a 1990 independence clause and claim to the disputed Karabakh region, saying it was the only way to reach a peace deal with Azerbaijan. The Caucasus foes have been locked in a territorial conflict over the mountainous region since the fall of the Soviet Union. In a 2023 offensive, Baku retook the Armenian-populated region, forcing a mass exodus, and has since demanded that Yerevan change its constitution for a peace treaty to be possible. Mr. Pashinyan addressed Armenians, promising a peace treaty with Azerbaijan should his countrymen back the new constitution in a referendum. Mr. Pashinyan said the new text rejects "the logic of the Declaration of Independence of August 23, 1990 — that is, the logic of conflict" and said the aim of the new constitution is to "ensure peace". The draft deletes the 1990 preamble, which included a clause for re-unification with the Nagorno-Karabakh region and called for the international recognition of the genocide of Armenians by the Ottoman Empire. Armenia's Opposition has accused Mr. Pashinyan of bowing to Azerbaijan's demands under pressure, calling it "Aliyev's Constitution" — after Azerbaijani leader Ilham Aliyev. But Mr. Pashinyan told Armenians not to believe "that we are doing this for someone else under external pressure". Mr. Pashinyan — whose party is several seats short of a constitutional majority in Parliament — called on the Opposition not to block the referendum.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: "If the people will vote against the constitution, I will resign," he said.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #24 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Armenia drops Nagorno-Karabakh claim in proposed new constitution

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 10:34:51 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The draft deletes the 1990 preamble, which included a clause for re-unification with the Nagorno-Karabakh region and called for the international recognition of the genocide of Armenians by the Ottoman Empire

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Armenian leader Nikol Pashinyan unveiled a draft constitution on Monday (November 23, 2026) that would get rid of a 1990 independence clause and claim to the disputed Karabakh region, saying it was the only way to reach a peace deal with Azerbaijan. The Caucasus foes have been locked in a territorial conflict over the mountainous region since the fall of the Soviet Union. In a 2023 offensive, Baku retook the Armenian-populated region, forcing a mass exodus, and has since demanded that Yerevan change its constitution for a peace treaty to be possible. Mr. Pashinyan addressed Armenians, promising a peace treaty with Azerbaijan should his countrymen back the new constitution in a referendum. Mr. Pashinyan said the new text rejects "the logic of the Declaration of Independence of August 23, 1990 — that is, the logic of conflict" and said the aim of the new constitution is to "ensure peace". The draft deletes the 1990 preamble, which included a clause for re-unification with the Nagorno-Karabakh region and called for the international recognition of the genocide of Armenians by the Ottoman Empire. Armenia's Opposition has accused Mr. Pashinyan of bowing to Azerbaijan's demands under pressure, calling it "Aliyev's Constitution" — after Azerbaijani leader Ilham Aliyev. But Mr. Pashinyan told Armenians not to believe "that we are doing this for someone else under external pressure". Mr. Pashinyan — whose party is several seats short of a constitutional majority in Parliament — called on the Opposition not to block the referendum.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: "If the people will vote against the constitution, I will resign," he said.

✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile

स्वतंत्रता — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Independence' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
Unification (Adjective / Verb)
एकीकरण — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Unification' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

articles.title: Zelenskyy hails Ukraine's attack on a Russian warship in Libya
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The operation, conducted some 2,400 kilometres (1,500 miles) from the front line in Ukraine, was the latest daring long-range assault by Kyiv's forces

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Ukraine carried out an attack on a Russian warship moored at a port in Libya, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Monday (November 23, 2026), claiming that maritime drones sank the navy vessel in a surprise assault the previous day. Ukrainian forces deployed seven drones in the operation that struck the Russian navy corvette in the Mediterranean, according to Mr. Zelenskyy. The ship, the Merkury, was one of Russia's newest vessels, commissioned a year after Moscow launched the 2022 full-scale invasion of its neighbor, he said in a post on X. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov declined to comment on the attack, saying that Russia's Defense Ministry would provide more information “if deemed to be appropriate.” The operation, conducted some 2,400 kilometres (1,500 miles) from the front line in Ukraine, was the latest daring long-range assault by Kyiv's forces. Ukraine has at times embarrassed Moscow during the war with attacks such as Operation Spiderweb in June 2025, when drones launched from trucks hit over 40 aircraft parked at air bases across Russia. Along the roughly 1,250-kilometre (almost 800-mile) front line snaking through eastern and southern Ukraine, Kyiv's drones and ground robots are helping hold back Russia's bigger army. At the same time, Russia's missiles and drones have devastated Ukraine's power grid ahead of winter and damaged civilian buildings. A Russian strike on a five-story apartment block in a village near Kyiv killed 11 people, regional police said on Monday (November 23, 2026). A 7-year-old child and a 79-year-old woman were pulled alive from the rubble after the Sunday (November 22, 2026) morning attack, rescue services said. Three people were killed on Monday (November 23, 2026) in a Russian strike on a hospital in the city of Zaporizhzhia in southern Ukraine, the regional military administration said. Two other people were killed when Russian forces struck a vehicle that bore markings indicating it was evacuating residents from the eastern city of Kramatorsk, authorities said. Mr. Zelenskyy described Sunday's (November 22, 2026) attack as “exemplary” and said “the targets we set were achieved.”
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “We continue our operations in designated waters. We are responding to Russia's aggression. We are developing Ukrainian weapons,” he said.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #24 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Zelenskyy hails Ukraine's attack on a Russian warship in Libya

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 10:27:47 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The operation, conducted some 2,400 kilometres (1,500 miles) from the front line in Ukraine, was the latest daring long-range assault by Kyiv's forces

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Ukraine carried out an attack on a Russian warship moored at a port in Libya, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Monday (November 23, 2026), claiming that maritime drones sank the navy vessel in a surprise assault the previous day. Ukrainian forces deployed seven drones in the operation that struck the Russian navy corvette in the Mediterranean, according to Mr. Zelenskyy. The ship, the Merkury, was one of Russia's newest vessels, commissioned a year after Moscow launched the 2022 full-scale invasion of its neighbor, he said in a post on X. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov declined to comment on the attack, saying that Russia's Defense Ministry would provide more information “if deemed to be appropriate.” The operation, conducted some 2,400 kilometres (1,500 miles) from the front line in Ukraine, was the latest daring long-range assault by Kyiv's forces. Ukraine has at times embarrassed Moscow during the war with attacks such as Operation Spiderweb in June 2025, when drones launched from trucks hit over 40 aircraft parked at air bases across Russia. Along the roughly 1,250-kilometre (almost 800-mile) front line snaking through eastern and southern Ukraine, Kyiv's drones and ground robots are helping hold back Russia's bigger army. At the same time, Russia's missiles and drones have devastated Ukraine's power grid ahead of winter and damaged civilian buildings. A Russian strike on a five-story apartment block in a village near Kyiv killed 11 people, regional police said on Monday (November 23, 2026). A 7-year-old child and a 79-year-old woman were pulled alive from the rubble after the Sunday (November 22, 2026) morning attack, rescue services said. Three people were killed on Monday (November 23, 2026) in a Russian strike on a hospital in the city of Zaporizhzhia in southern Ukraine, the regional military administration said. Two other people were killed when Russian forces struck a vehicle that bore markings indicating it was evacuating residents from the eastern city of Kramatorsk, authorities said. Mr. Zelenskyy described Sunday's (November 22, 2026) attack as “exemplary” and said “the targets we set were achieved.”

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “We continue our operations in designated waters. We are responding to Russia's aggression. We are developing Ukrainian weapons,” he said.

प्रशासन — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Administration' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
Aggression (Noun)
आक्रमण — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Aggression' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Operation (Noun)
संचालन — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Operation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🌐 International & Geopolitics passage on "Zelenskyy hails Ukraine's attack on a Russian warship in Libya", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The operation, conducted some 2,400 kilometres (1,500 miles) from the front line in Ukraine, was the latest daring long-range assault by Kyiv's forces.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Zelenskyy hails Ukraine's attack on a Russian wa' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Zelenskyy hails Ukraine's attack on a Russian' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Zelenskyy hails Ukraine's attack on a Russian' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The operation, conducted some 2,400 kilometres (1,500 miles) from the front line in Ukraine, was the latest daring long-range assault by Kyiv's forces." (Hinglish Arth: यूक्रेन में अग्रिम पंक्ति से लगभग 2,400 किलोमीटर (1,500 मील) दूर चलाया गया यह ऑपरेशन कीव की सेनाओं द्वारा किया गया नवीनतम साहसी लंबी दूरी का हमला था।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Zelenskyy hails Ukraine's attack on a Russian warship in Libya"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. We are developing Ukrainian weapons,” he said.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.

articles.title: India maps landslide susceptibility as part of shift from post-disaster relief to landslide management
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Mapping exercise covers 4.3 lakh square km; focus now on prevention, preparedness, risk reduction, says Science Minister; calls for interdisciplinary research, continuous monitoring to minimise impact

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: India has completed a national landslide susceptibility mapping exercise across approximately 4.3 lakh square kilometres, while the landslide inventory database has compiled information on nearly 91,000 historical landslides by the end of 2025, Minister for Science and Technology Jitendra Singh said on Monday (November 23, 2026). He noted that India is progressively shifting its approach to landslide management, from post-disaster relief to prevention, preparedness, and risk reduction, marking a “major transformation” in the country’s disaster management strategy. He was speaking at the 7th World Landslide Forum being held at the Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham, Faridabad. This is the first time the periodic International Consortium on Landslides and the International Programme on Landslides is being held in India. The 4-day programme brought together international experts, scientists, and policymakers from more than 75 countries. Recalling major landslide disasters in Kerala’s Wayanad and Uttarakhand’s Chamoli, as well as in Sikkim, Himachal Pradesh, and Jammu and Kashmir, Dr. Singh stressed the need for interdisciplinary research, continuous monitoring, and coordinated scientific efforts to minimise the impact of such disasters.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The National Landslide Forecasting Centre was established in Kolkata in 2024 and has now extended its activities to 20 districts, according to a statement from the Department of Science and Technology. The Regional Landslide Forecasting System, established in 2020, is supporting experimental and operational forecasting across vulnerable regions, it added.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #28 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 India maps landslide susceptibility as part of shift from post-disaster relief to landslide management

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 11:03:19 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Mapping exercise covers 4.3 lakh square km; focus now on prevention, preparedness, risk reduction, says Science Minister; calls for interdisciplinary research, continuous monitoring to minimise impact

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: India has completed a national landslide susceptibility mapping exercise across approximately 4.3 lakh square kilometres, while the landslide inventory database has compiled information on nearly 91,000 historical landslides by the end of 2025, Minister for Science and Technology Jitendra Singh said on Monday (November 23, 2026). He noted that India is progressively shifting its approach to landslide management, from post-disaster relief to prevention, preparedness, and risk reduction, marking a “major transformation” in the country’s disaster management strategy. He was speaking at the 7th World Landslide Forum being held at the Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham, Faridabad. This is the first time the periodic International Consortium on Landslides and the International Programme on Landslides is being held in India. The 4-day programme brought together international experts, scientists, and policymakers from more than 75 countries. Recalling major landslide disasters in Kerala’s Wayanad and Uttarakhand’s Chamoli, as well as in Sikkim, Himachal Pradesh, and Jammu and Kashmir, Dr. Singh stressed the need for interdisciplinary research, continuous monitoring, and coordinated scientific efforts to minimise the impact of such disasters.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The National Landslide Forecasting Centre was established in Kolkata in 2024 and has now extended its activities to 20 districts, according to a statement from the Department of Science and Technology. The Regional Landslide Forecasting System, established in 2020, is supporting experimental and operational forecasting across vulnerable regions, it added.

Recalling major landslide disasters in Kerala’s Wayanad and Uttarakhand’s Chamoli, as well as in Sikkim, Himachal Pradesh, and Jammu and Kashmir, Dr. Singh stressed the need for interdisciplinary research, continuous monitoring, and coordinated scientific efforts to minimise the impact of such disasters.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The National Landslide Forecasting Centre was established in Kolkata in 2024 and has now extended its activities to 20 districts, according to a statement from the Department of Science and Technology. The Regional Landslide Forecasting System, established in 2020, is supporting experimental and operational forecasting across vulnerable regions, it added.

articles.title: Wall Street roars back as Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Nvidia shares surged 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after an extraordinary reversal, which followed President Donald Trump’s call for Jensen Huang’s return

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Wall Street’s main indexes rallied sharply on Monday (November 23, 2026), led by a ​nearly 7% jump in the tech-heavy Nasdaq, as investors rushed back into AI-linked stocks ⁠after Nvidia said it had reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive. Nvidia shares surged 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after an extraordinary reversal, which followed President Donald Trump’s call for Mr. Huang’s return. Mr. Huang resigned ‌as chief executive earlier this month over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. The chipmaker is widely regarded as a cornerstone of the AI trade, and ‌its sharp rebound helped lift sentiment across the sector after weeks of heavy selling. “Huang’s return ‌marks ⁠one of the biggest reversals in the history of the stock market. Never has so ⁠much value rested on the shoulders of a single executive,” said David Russell, global head of market strategy at TradeStation. “Wall Street envisioned a stock market without his leadership and didn’t like what it saw.” The Nasdaq-100 was on track to add more than $2 trillion ​in market value on Monday (November 23). The Nasdaq ‌Composite and the S&P 500 were on track for their biggest one-day gains since markets surged after Mr. Trump paused his “Liberation Day” tariff package in April 2025. Chip stocks gained, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index up 13.4% and also on track for its best session since April 2025.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The rally was broad-based in ‌the tech sphere, with the so-called Magnificent Seven stocks Tesla, Amazon , Microsoft, Meta and Alphabet climbing ​between 5.8% and 12.4%.

📈 Economic, Banking & Finance Paragraph #13 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Wall Street roars back as Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 11:45:34 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Nvidia shares surged 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after an extraordinary reversal, which followed President Donald Trump’s call for Jensen Huang’s return

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Wall Street’s main indexes rallied sharply on Monday (November 23, 2026), led by a ​nearly 7% jump in the tech-heavy Nasdaq, as investors rushed back into AI-linked stocks ⁠after Nvidia said it had reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive. Nvidia shares surged 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after an extraordinary reversal, which followed President Donald Trump’s call for Mr. Huang’s return. Mr. Huang resigned ‌as chief executive earlier this month over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. The chipmaker is widely regarded as a cornerstone of the AI trade, and ‌its sharp rebound helped lift sentiment across the sector after weeks of heavy selling. “Huang’s return ‌marks ⁠one of the biggest reversals in the history of the stock market. Never has so ⁠much value rested on the shoulders of a single executive,” said David Russell, global head of market strategy at TradeStation. “Wall Street envisioned a stock market without his leadership and didn’t like what it saw.” The Nasdaq-100 was on track to add more than $2 trillion ​in market value on Monday (November 23). The Nasdaq ‌Composite and the S&P 500 were on track for their biggest one-day gains since markets surged after Mr. Trump paused his “Liberation Day” tariff package in April 2025. Chip stocks gained, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index up 13.4% and also on track for its best session since April 2025.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The rally was broad-based in ‌the tech sphere, with the so-called Magnificent Seven stocks Tesla, Amazon , Microsoft, Meta and Alphabet climbing ​between 5.8% and 12.4%.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Karnataka needs a coherent policy on urban mobility

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: While Karnataka has spent years disputing motorcycle owners’ right to carry paying passengers, Bengaluru — with the dubious distinction of having one of the world’s highest travel times per unit distance — struggles with inadequate public transport capacity and lacklustre intermediate options. The Supreme Court ruling on November 20 to dismiss Karnataka’s appeal was thus straightforward, allowing motorcycles to be registered as transport vehicles. The State has often called bike taxis unsafe, yet has not improved the prospects of safer options. Earlier this year, the Centre for Science and Environment estimated the number of buses in urban centres nationwide to be 70% short of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs benchmark and that 400 cities with populations between a lakh and 10 lakh altogether lacked organised bus services. In March, the BMTC reported a fleet of around 7,000 buses in Bengaluru, versus the 13,000 by 2025 envisaged by the Comprehensive Mobility Plan. Expanding the number of Metro stations also creates more demand for travel to and from stations, but the operating costs of the public transport corporation expected to serve that demand are not covered by the resulting increase in rail ridership. Overall, Karnataka has struggled to set up a consistent transport policy. An expert committee recommended against bike taxis in Bengaluru for first- and last-mile connectivity and in favour of better walking infrastructure and bicycle rentals in 2019, only for the State to launch the electric bike-taxi scheme in 2021, then rescind it in 2024 over safety concerns and drivers’ disputes. The market for short booked journeys is also dysfunctional. But while allowing bike taxis could temper autorickshaw fares, the State must investigate drivers’ operating costs, the difference between the paid and the received amounts, and prevent large platforms from exploiting the market. Finally, while the Union Road Transport Ministry has reported that 46.2% of all road deaths involved two-wheeler users, two-wheelers’ safety relative to autorickshaws and cabs, by the number and distance of journeys, is unclear. The State should require aggregators to report injuries and fatalities and investigate the consequences of drivers’ earnings being linked to the number of trips undertaken. The Union government’s 2025 Motor Vehicle Aggregator Guidelines already address passenger security, fares, and insurance while allowing States to authorise privately registered motorcycles through aggregators. Karnataka should exercise this additional power. A large national programme is required to address funding for public transport, which is necessary even when it is not immediately profitable.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Karnataka / scooters and motorbikes / public transport / court / population / urban planning / Bengaluru Metro / Electric vehicles / road accident / road transport / insurance

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Developed nations must bear much of the cost of carbon emissions

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: COP31 ended in Antalya, Türkiye, with a whimper. The 190-odd countries that had convened for nearly 12 days — a close to 50-hour overshoot — failed to agree on an overarching political statement , called a cover text, that acts as a stepping stone to future, collective global action on climate change. Usually, cover texts evolve as a final synthesis of deliberations ; the COP31 leadership, helmed by Türkiye and Australia, thought it fit to push for a cover text early in the proceedings. The headline sought was a global electrification target: 35% of global final energy consumption will come from electricity by 2035, in the hope that this would reduce direct fossil fuel emissions. Ultimately, the cover text failed to pass muster because the European Union objected to the text’s lack of any explicit mention of ‘fossil fuel,’ let alone its phase-out. The COP process is arduously protracted as even a single country’s objection can stall progress. Country-blocks outside the EU, such as coalitions of the least developed countries, island nations, some South American countries — reportedly 130 countries — were also insistent on fossil fuel language. While COP 31 made some progress on old pathways, such as the Just Transition agreement, it is perplexing that the delegations could not make progress on the other big prong of negotiations: climate finance. The increase in solar panel installations and the significant shift towards battery use in grid storage and transport did not come cheap: the cost of the land required for their installation, their intermittent nature of being dependent on weather, grid upgrades all carry costs. It is global markets, imperfectly connected, but connected, that have managed to bring it to this stage over decades. India and China, major fossil emitters, with large, still indigent populations, are also leaders in total clean energy installations. Therefore it stands to reason that developed countries, which have committed to providing climate finance in recognition of their historical emissions, make good on past promises to shoulder the cost of the carbon emissions that are responsible for warming. Economic crises are a feature, and not a bug, of the interconnected financial system enveloping the world and there are, undeniably, challenges to diverting the necessary finance towards countries most vulnerable to climate change impact. However, it is no longer prudent to sweep this under the rug by scuttling experimental approaches — namely carbon capture — as inimical to the broader commitment to eschew fossil fuel. When the primary framework climate agreement was crafted three decades ago, nobody envisaged AI and the drain that data centres portended or the wars that would see the vociferous antagonists of coal immediately shore up their gas reserves. Without honest good-faith dialogue, the COP is at risk of being a sideshow: a mortal blow to multilateralism.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: climate change / Turkey / politics / Australia / electricity production and distribution / energy and resource / European Union / solar / India / China / carbon emissions / population / economy / carbon capture and sequestration / Artificial Intelligence / data management storage

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Rohingya cannot return unless Myanmar turns democratic

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: On November 19, the International Court of Justice held that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya. It is for the first time that the court has found any state responsible for the crime. The verdict, with nine votes to six, was not lightly reached. Genocide requires proof of an intent to destroy a group. In the absence of direct evidence of a plan, the court could infer that intent only if it was “the only reasonable inference” from the facts, a high bar to affix responsibility. The facts it accepted are harrowing. In 2017, in what Myanmar’s army called “clearance operations” against the insurgent Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army, at least 10,000 Rohingya were killed, 1,834 raped and 392 villages destroyed in northern Rakhine State. Over 7,00,000 fled to Bangladesh. Then Army chief Min Aung Hlaing, now Myanmar’s “civilian” President, called the “Bengali problem” an “unfinished job”. Myanmar argued that it had only been fighting insurgents or at worst, driving the Rohingya out or punishing them. The court said that the army drew no distinction between fighters and civilians, had no plan to move anyone, fired on fleeing people and killed children on a scale that could not be explained as punishment. Seen alongside decades of discrimination, the evidence pointed to an intent to destroy. The incidents of 2017 were no aberration. The army drove lakhs of Rohingya into Bangladesh in 1978 and 1991-92. The junta stripped the Rohingya of citizenship in 1982 and the state branded them as “foreigners” in Arakan, disenfranchising them in 2015. While the junta’s Bamar-Buddhist vision has oppressed every minority, the Rohingya have been subjected to the most brutality. More than 1.2 million are in Bangladesh, living in dilapidated conditions, made worse due to diminished international aid. The court ordered Myanmar to allow their safe, voluntary and dignified return and to compensate them, but it has no means of enforcing its judgment. Only the UN Security Council can, but it will be subject to vetoes by Myanmar’s backers, China and Russia. On the very day of the verdict, the two joined the U.S. in Shenzhen to declare the “immunities of State officials” of “paramount importance”. Others, India among them, have courted the regime in Naypyitaw regardless, following sham elections that made the junta leader civilian President earlier this year. And Rakhine State, mired in civil war, is now mostly held by the Arakan Army which is accused of atrocities against the Rohingya. Only a truly democratic, federal, plural and peaceful Myanmar can bring the Rohingya home in safety.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: international court or tribunal / Myanmar / Rohingya crisis / crime / armed Forces / sexual assault / Bangladesh / Citizenship / welfare / United Nations / China / Russia / India / democracy

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Even a low base effect could not push India’s oil and gas sectors into growth

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The core sector performance in October is a good example of how statistical distortions can create incorrect assessments of the economy. The 10.9% growth rate, a series high, has been celebrated as a sign of the Indian economy’s strength and resilience. There is, no doubt, an aspect of this has been reflected in the numbers, especially to do with infrastructure creation. However, the much more impactful factor behind the high core sector growth was a low base effect. The overall Index of Core Industries grew just 0.8% in October 2025 and so, in relation, the performance in October 2026 looked that much faster. This low base effect is even starker when looking at individual sectors within the index. The coal sector grew at a blistering 23% in October, more than twice its growth rate in the previous month. Yet, a large part of this was propelled by the fact that the sector had contracted nearly 8.5% last October. The rest of the sector’s growth was driven by demand of the electricity and iron ore sectors, or so the data show. The electricity sector also grew at a series high of nearly 22% in October, but on the back of a near-7% contraction in October last year. This base effect anomaly is likely down to the fact that the festive season starts at different but similar points every year. As such, a more accurate reading of the economy will be possible once the data for November are available.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The construction-related sectors seem to have seen genuine growth, a reflection of the government’s ongoing infrastructure push. The iron ore sector’s growth rate accelerated to a three-month high of 26.4% in October 2026 as compared to a growth of 8.7% in the same month last year. Steel grew at 7.3% versus 9.5% last year, and cement by 15.4% versus 5.2%. The economy’s dependence on government spending is not going to ease in the near future, and might even intensify as higher costs eat into companies’ profit margins. The core sector data once again highlighted a major reason for these higher costs — the oil and gas sectors. The crude oil sector shrank by 4.1%, its 22nd consecutive month of contraction. The natural gas sector, similarly, contracted 7.6%, a series-worst performance and the 28th straight month of contraction. A major reason behind high inflation in India is the underperformance of these two sectors and the resultant dependence on imported fuel. It is time the Petroleum Ministry candidly explains — to Parliament in December or to the public directly — why India’s fuel output has been continuously falling. If it is a matter of a lack of resources underground, that is one thing, but the underperformance of oil and gas public sector undertakings is quite another. Accountability needs to be set.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Climate action has to be timely, with adequate resources and monitoring

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: That all was not well with the Green India Mission was clear even before its approval. After the UPA-I government announced it in 2008, the Ministry of Rural Development had objected to its financial design much before the Union Cabinet approved it in 2014. But the Environment Ministry proceeded anyway and retained largely the same arrangement when it revised the Mission in 2021. Following the Comptroller and Auditor General’s report, on November 19, the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) upbraided the Ministry for the Mission’s virtual failure and for still not having issued the implementation guidelines for the revised form. The original 10-year vision was to expand forest and tree cover by 5 million hectares (mha), improve forest quality on another 5 mha, improve forest-related livelihoods for 3 million households, and sequester up to 60 million tonnes of carbon dioxide a year. The outlay was ₹46,000 crore. In 2014, the Cabinet approved ₹13,000 crore for 1.4 mha each of the first two objectives by 2018, but to be supported to the tune of 81.5% by Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority (CAMPA), National Afforestation Programme (NAP), and MGNREGS funds. In 2021-22, the Ministry folded the NAP into the Mission and, in mid-2025, unveiled a revised version with an allocation of ₹12,190 crore to improve forest cover on 25 mha by 2030, including 24 mha through other schemes. The government had thus expanded the primary target but left the Mission responsible for only 1 mha.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Together with the CAMPA, NAP, and MGNREGS funds never materialising, it is no surprise that the programmes to improve forest quality and forest cover have respectively fallen short by 91.8% and 97.5% vis-à-vis the 2014 target. The Environment Ministry had assembled a large programme around resources that it knew it could not control. Pro-climate work in practice ought to span government schemes to deliver action and justice, and the Ministry ought to have formalised the division of responsibilities and accounting system. The PAC’s new demand that the Ministry submit an implementation timetable is insufficient. From the Jal Shakti Abhiyan in 2019 to the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan in 2024, the government has often floated new programmes banking significantly on funds from existing schemes — an untenable policy when the latter also have their own obligations. And if the VB-G RAM G scheme was to also advance climate justice, the government should not have undermined the erstwhile demand-driven funding model and shifted more financial responsibility to the States. Climate action has to be timely, for which the Union government must dedicate adequate resources and proactively ensure that its initiatives are implemented.

1. Core Context & Background: Saurav Das was served the notice at 7.30 p.m. by email on November 23, hours before his flight; the government has not issued any statement on the reasons for stopping him at the Delhi airport

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Saurav Das, co-convenor of the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), was stopped from boarding a flight to London at Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International Airport (IGI) on Monday night (November 23, 2026) after failing to respond to a show-cause notice issued by the Regional Passport Office (RPO), Chennai, over alleged discrepancies between his passport and other identity documents, a senior government official told The Hindu . His passport was issued in 2019 and the notice was served at 7.30 p.m. by email on November 23, hours before he was to board the flight at 1 a.m. on November 24. The government has issued no official statement on the reasons for stopping him at the airport. According to the notice, the RPO, Chennai, said that it has received inputs about Mr. Das’ passport application dated August 8, 2019, stating that “particulars (place of birth) furnished in it are incorrect” and his passport dated August 21, 2019 was “obtained by material suppression of facts.” “You are hereby called upon to provide a suitable clarification with respect to your place of birth along with supporting documents within seven days. Failure to produce a satisfactory response or a lack of response may result in impounding of your passport under Section 10(3)(b) of the Passports Act, 1967. You are advised not to use this passport till submission of response,” the notice seen by The Hindu said. Mr. Das said he saw the email with a show-cause notice about “discrepancies” in his passport only after he was stopped at the immigration counter at the Delhi airport. “I have no issue in providing any explanation. But I only received a show-cause notice five hours prior to my flight scheduled at 1 a.m. I did not see it before I was stopped at the airport. It says they have received an input over mismatch in my data. Can a citizen be stopped from travelling on such an input without disclosing any details of it?” He questioned why no issue was flagged in the verification process when an Indian passport was issued to him in 2019. “I have travelled abroad twice since without being stopped. The issue is being raised this time because I am associated with the CJP movement. My place of birth, my parents are being dragged into this. But we are not scared of cheap tactics.” The notice followed a September 30 order by the Madras High Court , which acted on a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) petition seeking a probe by the Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) into the nationality of Mr. Das and sought to cancel his passport and Aadhaar card if he is not found to be an Indian. The First Division Bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan also ordered notice to Mr. Das on the PIL petition filed by R. Ganesh Kumar, a businessman from Chennai. The official said that Mr. Das was asked to explain why his passport should not be impounded, as there is a mismatch in documents submitted to obtain his passport and Aadhaar. “There appears to be a mismatch regarding his date of birth, place of birth and name of father in various documents — Aadhaar, birth certificate and passport. He was asked by the RPO, Chennai to explain his stance but he did not, following which his passport was flagged and he was stopped by the immigration,” said the official.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Addressing a press conference in Delhi, Mr. Das said, “Let alone being stopped from going abroad, we have not been allowed to speak inside the country. We were stopped from going to Jantar Mantar and then Ramlila Maidan. When we took to online spaces, attempts to stop were made even there.”

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Madurai Collector submitted before the Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court that the administration was taking steps to comply with the Supreme Court order

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Defying the Supreme Court’s direction to allow, as a “limited one-time arrangement”, the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at the newly identified deepathoon on Thirupparankundram hillock, the ceremonial lamp was on Tuesday lit only at the traditional spot. Earlier in the day, the Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court had recorded an undertaking by Madurai Collector Nishant Krishna that he will continue to act in strict compliance with the Supreme Court’s orders. The failure to fulfil this undertaking triggered massive protest by the leaders and cadres of the BJP and Hindu outfits at the foothills, while the ruling TVK’s allies, including the Left parties, the VCK, and the MDMK, hailed the government for sticking to tradition. “The Karthigai Mahadeepam has been lit in the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchchipillaiyar Temple located directly above the head of the presiding deity at Thirupparankundram,” Law Minister C.T.R. Nirmal Kumar said in a social media post. Shortly after the Deepam was lit, the Executive Officer of Arulmigu Subramaniya Swamy Temple, G. Selvi, and Board of Trustees Chairman V. Shanmugasundaram, in a joint press release, said the temple followed the age-old practice and agama rules in lighting the lamp. The Board of Trustees, including C. Rajapandian, K. Alagappan, K. Regina Devi, and K. Chitra, passed a resolution unanimously, resolving to follow the rituals and ensure the festival is conducted in a peaceful environment. The press release said the temple, known as the first abode of Lord Muruga (Arupadai Veedu), had been following the rituals from time immemorial. The temple, which has been conducting various festivals all through the year, adopted custom and rituals and age old continued practice as per the agama rules. In line with this, the Deepam was lit as per the old practice at the designated deepa mandapam atop the Uchipillayar temple and the light was lit at 6 p.m., the release said. The district administration, in a statement, said all arrangements were made as directed by the Supreme Court. The temple Devasthanam was requested, instructed in writing, and reminded to authorise its team and proceed. However, the Devasthanam did not authorise a team till the last moment. Instead, its Board of Trustees passed a resolution to light the lamp at the usual place, and the lamp was lit at the Deepa Mandapam, it added. Earlier, the police detained several senior leaders of the BJP, including State president Nainar Nagenthran, and Hindu outfits to prevent them from proceeding to Thirupparankundram.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Thousands of police personnel, deployed for security at the foothills, detained protesters and took them away. A section of the protesters damaged buses and other public property.
